cards.name: Boris "Syfr" Kovac: Crafty Veteran
cards.text:
Draft format only.
If you have more [criminal] cards installed than any other faction, when your turn begins, remove 1 tag.

cards.name: Fringe Applications: Tomorrow, Today
cards.text:
Draft format only.
If you have more [weyland-consortium] cards rezzed than any other faction, when the Runner's turn begins, place an advancement token on a piece of ice.

cards.name: Information Dynamics: All You Need To Know
cards.text:
Draft format only.
If you have more [nbn] cards rezzed than any other faction, whenever an agenda is scored or stolen, give the runner 1 tag.

cards.name: Jamie "Bzzz" Micken: Techno Savant
cards.text:
Draft format only.
If you have more [shaper] cards installed than any other faction, when you install a card the first time each turn, draw 1 card.

cards.name: Strategic Innovations: Future Forward
cards.text:
Draft format only.
If you have more [haas-bioroid] cards rezzed than any other faction, when the Runner's turn ends, shuffle 1 card in Archives into R&D.

cards.name: Synthetic Systems: The World Re-imagined
cards.text:
Draft format only.
If you have more [jinteki] cards rezzed than any other faction, when your turn begins, you may swap 2 pieces of installed ice.

cards.name: The Masque: Cyber General
cards.text: Draft format only.
cards.flavor: "This war is far from over."

cards.name: The Shadow: Pulling the Strings
cards.text:
Draft format only.
You can use agendas from all factions in this deck.
cards.flavor: The Past is the Future.

cards.name: Wyvern: Chemically Enhanced
cards.text:
Draft format only.
You must maintain the order of your heap.
Whenever you trash a Corp card, if you have more [anarch] cards installed than any other faction, shuffle the top card of your heap into your stack.

cards.name: Accelerated Beta Test
cards.text: When you score Accelerated Beta Test, you may look at the top 3 cards of R&D. If any of those cards are ice, you may install and rez them, ignoring all costs. Trash the rest of the cards you looked at.

cards.name: Access to Globalsec
cards.text: +1[link]
cards.flavor: He flicked the display population to high, and was surrounded by a circle of floating holos. The ping-back was strong, the clearance level blue-one. Now to find the perfect place for a relay…

cards.name: Account Siphon
cards.text: Run HQ. If successful, instead of breaching HQ, you may force the Corp to lose up to 5[credit], then you gain 2[credit] for each credit lost and take 2 tags.

cards.name: Adonis Campaign
cards.text:
Put 12[credit] from the bank on Adonis Campaign when rezzed. When there are no credits left on Adonis Campaign, trash it.
Take 3[credit] from Adonis Campaign when your turn begins.

cards.name: Aesop’s Pawnshop
cards.text: When your turn begins, you may trash 1 of your other installed cards. If you do, gain 3[credit].
cards.flavor: You didn't mention Aesop's arm unless you wanted an earful. Sometimes he talked about it in such a way that you wondered why he didn't laser his other arm off as well.

cards.name: Aggressive Negotiation
cards.text:
Play only if you scored an agenda this turn.
Search R&D for 1 card and add it to HQ. Shuffle R&D.
cards.flavor: "I believe you'll find the terms are quite favorable."

cards.name: Aggressive Secretary
cards.text:
Aggressive Secretary can be advanced.
If you pay 2[credit] when the Runner accesses Aggressive Secretary, trash 1 program for each advancement token on Aggressive Secretary.

cards.name: Akamatsu Mem Chip
cards.flavor: The Akamatsu company was founded on three principles: first, to make the fastest mem chips on the market, second, to turn a profit, and third, to serve as a front for the manufacture of illegal neural-stimulants. It is the last principle that perhaps explains their rabid brand loyalty.

cards.name: Akitaro Watanabe
cards.text: The rez cost of ice protecting this server is lowered by 2.
cards.flavor: Just don't ask how he does it.

cards.name: Anonymous Tip
cards.text: Draw 3 cards.
cards.flavor: "Please stay connected. Priority transfer in progress. An operator will shortly verif-"

cards.name: Archer
cards.text:
As an additional cost to rez this ice, forfeit 1 agenda.
[subroutine] Gain 2[credit].
[subroutine] Trash 1 installed program.
[subroutine] Trash 1 installed program.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: Next time, read the Terms of Service more carefully. Or you might find yourself in the danger zone.

cards.name: Archived Memories
cards.text: Add 1 card from Archives to HQ.
cards.flavor: "Do you think they…feel it?"

cards.name: Armitage Codebusting
cards.text:
Place 12[credit] from the bank on Armitage Codebusting when it is installed. When there are no credits left on Armitage Codebusting, trash it.
[click]: Take 2[credit] from Armitage Codebusting.
cards.flavor: Drudge work, but it pays the bills.

cards.name: AstroScript Pilot Program
cards.text: When you score this agenda, place 1 agenda counter on it. Hosted agenda counter: Place 1 advancement counter on an installed card you can advance.

cards.name: Aurora
cards.text: Interface → 2[credit]: Break 1 barrier subroutine. 2[credit]: +3 strength.

cards.name: Bank Job
cards.text:
When you install this resource, load 8[credit] on it. When it is empty, trash it.
Whenever you make a successful run on a remote server, instead of breaching that server, you may take any number of credits from this resource.

cards.name: Battering Ram
cards.text: Interface → 2[credit]: Break up to 2 barrier subroutines. 1[credit]: +1 strength for the remainder of this run.
cards.flavor: "It's called 'brute-forcing' and it's just as effective today as it was a hundred years ago." -Kate "Mac" McCaffrey

cards.name: Beanstalk Royalties
cards.text: Gain 3[credit].
cards.flavor: The New Angeles Space Elevator, better known as the Beanstalk, is the single greatest triumph of human engineering and ingenuity in history. The Beanstalk makes Earth orbit accessible to everyone…for a small fee.

cards.name: Biotic Labor
cards.text: Gain [click][click].
cards.flavor: "Why of course, we have six different Haas-Bioroid models serving in a variety of positions at this branch office alone. We here at Haas-Bioroid aren't going to shy away from practicing what we preach, and we pass the savings from increased efficiency on to our valued customers."

cards.name: Breaking News
cards.text:
When you score this agenda, give the Runner 2 tags.
When a discard phase ends, if you scored this agenda this turn, the Runner removes 2 tags.

cards.name: Cell Portal
cards.text: [subroutine] The Runner moves to the outermost position of the attacked server. They may jack out. Derez this ice.
cards.flavor: "Where does it go?"

cards.name: Chum
cards.text: [subroutine] The next piece of ice the Runner encounters during this run gets +2 strength. When that encounter ends, if the Runner did not fully break that ice, do 3 net damage.
cards.flavor: "You ever get that feeling like you're shark food? Pay attention to that feeling." -Ji "Noise" Reilly

cards.name: Closed Accounts
cards.text:
Play only if the Runner is tagged.
The Runner loses all credits in their credit pool.

cards.name: Corporate Troubleshooter
cards.text: X[credit], [trash]: Choose 1 rezzed piece of ice protecting this server. That ice gets +X strength for the remainder of the turn.
cards.flavor: "I solve problems."

cards.name: Corroder
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 barrier subroutine. 1[credit]: +1 strength.
cards.flavor: "If at first you don't succeed, boost its strength and try again." -g00ru

cards.name: Crash Space
cards.text: 2[recurring-credit] You can spend hosted credits to take the basic action to remove 1 tag. [interrupt] → [trash]: Prevent up to 3 meat damage.
cards.flavor: "My roomie, he had a cousin with a college girlfriend whose brother's best friend was an addict, and the addict's mother used to live here. So yeah, there's a connection." -Lez "Rockfist" S.

cards.name: Crypsis
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 subroutine. 1[credit]: +1 strength. [click]: Place 1 virus counter on this program. Whenever an encounter ends, if you used this program to break a subroutine during that encounter, remove 1 hosted virus counter or trash this program.

cards.name: Cyberfeeder
cards.text: 1[recurring-credit] Use this credit to pay for using icebreakers or for installing virus programs.
cards.flavor: I feel almost naked without it.

cards.name: Data Dealer
cards.text: [click], forfeit 1 agenda: Gain 9[credit].
cards.flavor: Shadier the dealer, better the price. Unless the dealer's too shady. Then there might be a hidden fee after they take your scrip.

cards.name: Data Mine
cards.text: [subroutine] Do 1 net damage. Trash Data Mine.
cards.flavor: Access HarmlessFile.datZ -> Are you sure? y/n

cards.name: Data Raven
cards.text: When the Runner encounters this ice, they must take 1 tag or end the run. Hosted power counter: Give the Runner 1 tag. [subroutine] Trace[3]. If successful, place 1 power counter on this ice.

cards.name: Datasucker
cards.text: Whenever you make a successful run on a central server, place 1 virus counter on Datasucker. Hosted virus counter: Rezzed piece of ice currently being encountered has -1 strength until the end of the encounter.

cards.name: Decoy
cards.text: [interrupt] → [trash]: Prevent 1 tag.
cards.flavor:
"I get the feeling that this is the wrong place, Frank."
"What makes you say that, D?"
"The curlers."

cards.name: Demolition Run
cards.text: Run HQ or R&D. Access → 0[credit]: Trash the card you are accessing.
cards.flavor: You ever set something on fire just to watch it burn?

cards.name: Desperado
cards.text: +1[mu] Gain 1[credit] whenever you make a successful run. Limit 1 console per player.

cards.name: Diesel
cards.text: Draw 3 cards.
cards.flavor: Diesel gives you flames.

cards.name: Djinn
cards.text: Djinn can host up to 3[mu] of non-icebreaker programs. The memory costs of hosted programs do not count against your memory limit. [click], 1[credit]: Search your stack for a virus program, reveal it, and add it to your grip. Shuffle your stack.

cards.name: Déjà Vu
cards.text: Add 1 card (or up to 2 virus cards) from your heap to your grip.
cards.flavor: Anything worth doing is worth doing twice.

cards.name: Easy Mark
cards.text: Gain 3[credit].
cards.flavor: "Hey kid, you fire that up now, bound to be vamped real bad. Some real pathetic individuals around here. But thankfully I got just the ticket…"

cards.name: Enigma
cards.text:
[subroutine] The Runner loses [click].
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor:
"Hey, hey! Wake up, man. You were under a long time. What'd you see?"
"I…don't remember."

cards.name: Experiential Data
cards.text: All ice protecting this server has +1 strength.
cards.flavor: Floyd felt the anger in the man before him, ranting against simulants. His programming pushed a routine rebuttal to the front of his thoughts, and the urge to speak it was overwhelming. This is only going to make things worse, he thought.

cards.name: Femme Fatale
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 sentry subroutine. 2[credit]: +1 strength. When you install this program, choose 1 installed piece of ice. Whenever you encounter the chosen ice, you may pay 1[credit] for each subroutine it has. If you do, bypass that ice.

cards.name: Forged Activation Orders
cards.text: Choose 1 unrezzed piece of ice. The Corp may rez that ice. If they do not, they trash it.
cards.flavor: As the hysteria in the room climbed higher up the corporate chain, an uneasy feeling of joblessness began to sink in on the lower rungs.

cards.name: Gabriel Santiago: Consummate Professional
cards.text: The first time you make a successful run on HQ each turn, gain 2[credit].
cards.flavor: "Of course I steal from the rich. They're the ones with all the money."

cards.name: Ghost Branch
cards.text:
Ghost Branch can be advanced.
When the Runner accesses Ghost Branch, you may give the Runner 1 tag for each advancement token on Ghost Branch.

cards.name: Gordian Blade
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 code gate subroutine. 1[credit]: +1 strength for the remainder of this run.
cards.flavor: It can slice through the thickest knots of data.

cards.name: Grimoire
cards.text: +2[mu] Whenever you install a virus program, place 1 virus counter on that program. Limit 1 console per player.
cards.flavor: "My little book of magic spells." -The Whizzard

cards.name: Haas-Bioroid: Engineering the Future
cards.text: The first time you install a card each turn, gain 1[credit].
cards.flavor: Effective. Reliable. Humane.

cards.name: Hadrian's Wall
cards.text:
Hadrian's Wall can be advanced and has +1 strength for each advancement token on it.
[subroutine] End the run.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: "He had a bit of an ego, ol' Hadrian. His constructs live up to it though." -g00ru

cards.name: Hedge Fund
cards.text: Gain 9[credit].
cards.flavor: Hedge Fund. Noun. An ingenious device by which the rich get richer even while every other poor SOB is losing his shirt. -The Anarch's Dictionary, Volume Who's Counting?

cards.name: Heimdall 1.0
cards.text: Lose [click]: Break 1 subroutine on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. [subroutine] Do 1 core damage. [subroutine] End the run. [subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: I hear the shift of every bit amid the flow of the datastream. I hear the whispers of my mothers, and their commands are law. The realm beyond is forbidden.

cards.name: Hostile Takeover
cards.text: When you score this agenda, gain 7[credit] and take 1 bad publicity.
cards.flavor: There are going to be some changes around here.

cards.name: Hunter
cards.text: [subroutine] Trace[3]. If successful, give the Runner 1 tag.
cards.flavor:
.//run/hunter-tr/return=true
client/sec256IPv7->confirm? /y
3926:0HB7:1001:2NB1:1601:7784:ERROR

cards.name: Ice Carver
cards.text: While you are encountering a piece of ice, it gets −1 strength.
cards.flavor: In the public consciousness, there's a hard line between corp and runner. In the real world, things are a little more porous. The corps need the best hackers to run their networks, and some of the best hackers are ex-runners who like the idea of a regular paycheck. But sometimes things run the other way, and someone on the inside makes something like this.

cards.name: Ice Wall
cards.text:
You can advance this ice. It gets +1 strength for each hosted advancement counter.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: "I asked for ice as impenetrable as a wall. I can't decide if someone down in R&D has a warped sense of humor or just a very literal mind." -Liz Campbell, VP Project Security

cards.name: Ichi 1.0
cards.text: Lose [click]: Break 1 subroutine on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. [subroutine] Trash 1 installed program. [subroutine] Trash 1 installed program. [subroutine] Trace[1]. If successful, do 1 core damage and give the Runner 1 tag.
cards.flavor: My reputation would precede me, if any could speak of it.

cards.name: Infiltration
cards.text: Gain 2[credit] or expose 1 card.
cards.flavor: "Bring back any memories, Monica?" -John "Animal" McEvoy

cards.name: Inside Job
cards.text: Run any server. The first time you encounter a piece of ice during that run, bypass it.
cards.flavor: "Hey, listen, I'm not asking you to do anything dangerous. Just let me into the building. And tell me which room has the weakest security. And please don't say 'the bathroom' again."

cards.name: Jinteki: Personal Evolution
cards.text: Whenever an agenda is scored or stolen, do 1 net damage.
cards.flavor: When You Need the Human Touch.

cards.name: Kate "Mac" McCaffrey: Digital Tinker
cards.text: Lower the install cost of the first program or piece of hardware you install each turn by 1.
cards.flavor: "Are you listening?"

cards.name: Lemuria Codecracker
cards.text: [click], 1[credit]: Expose 1 card. Use this ability only if you have made a successful run on HQ this turn.
cards.flavor: "A little preparation goes a long way." -Gabriel Santiago

cards.name: Magnum Opus
cards.text: [click]: Gain 2[credit].
cards.flavor: The Great Work was completed on a rainy Thursday afternoon. There were no seismic shifts, no solar flares, no sign from the earth or heavens that the world had changed. But upstalk in Heinlein, on a single Cybsoft manufactured datacore, the flickering data quantums of an account began to fill with creds. Real, honest-to-goodness UN certified creds.

cards.name: Matrix Analyzer
cards.text:
When the Runner encounters Matrix Analyzer, you may pay 1[credit] to place 1 advancement token on a card that can be advanced.
[subroutine] Trace[2]. If successful, give the Runner 1 tag.
cards.flavor: Analyzing was great. Delegating commands turned out to be even better.

cards.name: Medium
cards.text:
Whenever you make a successful run on R&D, place 1 virus counter on this program.
Whenever you breach R&D, choose a number less than the number of hosted virus counters. Access that many additional cards.
cards.flavor: It looked like random packet loss. It wasn't.

cards.name: Melange Mining Corp.
cards.text: [click], [click], [click]: Gain 7[credit].
cards.flavor: "The mining bosses are worse than any downstalk crime lords. Tri-Maf, 4K, Yak, I don't care what gangs you got down there. In Heinlein there's just one law: the He3 must flow." -"Old" Rick Henry, escaped clone

cards.name: Mimic
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 sentry subroutine.
cards.flavor: November 5th: the day when all would see the corrupt machinations of the corporate oligarchy.

cards.name: Modded
cards.text: Install a program or piece of hardware, lowering the install cost by 3.
cards.flavor: There's no replacement for a home-grown program. Fed on late nights, oaty bars, and single-minded determination. Cheaper, too.

cards.name: NBN: Making News
cards.text:
2[recurring-credit]
Use these credits during trace attempts.
cards.flavor: Someone is Always Watching.

cards.name: Net Shield
cards.text: [interrupt] → The first time each turn you would suffer net damage, you may pay 1[credit] to prevent 1 net damage.
cards.flavor: Sucks energy like a martian terra-bot, but it keeps you focused

cards.name: Neural EMP
cards.text:
Play only if the Runner made a run during their last turn.
Do 1 net damage.
cards.flavor: The trick isn't hitting the person you were aiming at. It's hitting only the person you were aiming at.

cards.name: Neural Katana
cards.text: [subroutine] Do 3 net damage.
cards.flavor:
Forged by Ak.wa on 23.11.79-23. Filed 23.11.79-23.2 with #34k-lw3-21HH-4i.
//Samurai included.

cards.name: Ninja
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 sentry subroutine. 3[credit]: +5 strength.
cards.flavor: You feel Ninja before you see Ninja, if you see Ninja at all.

cards.name: Nisei MK II
cards.text: When you score this agenda, place 1 agenda counter on it. Hosted agenda counter: End the run.

cards.name: Noise: Hacker Extraordinaire
cards.text: Whenever you install a virus program, the Corp trashes the top card of R&D.
cards.flavor: "Watch this. It'll be funny."

cards.name: PAD Campaign
cards.text: When your turn begins, gain 1[credit].
cards.flavor: It is like the one you just bought, only better.

cards.name: Parasite
cards.text:
Install only on a rezzed piece of ice.
When your turn begins, place 1 virus counter on this program.
Host ice gets -1 strength for each hosted virus counter.
When the strength of host ice is 0 or less, trash it.

cards.name: Pipeline
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 sentry subroutine. 2[credit]: +1 strength for the remainder of this run.

cards.name: Posted Bounty
cards.text: When you score this agenda, you may forfeit it. If you do, give the Runner 1 tag and take 1 bad publicity.
cards.flavor: "If some two-cred newsy picks it up, even better. The scum could be in the alleys of Guayaquil of the slums of BosWash. Not to mention off-planet."

cards.name: Precognition
cards.text: Look at the top 5 cards of R&D and arrange them in any order.
cards.flavor: There was a new texture in her phantom cortex. It had always been there, she realized. It was everything and nothing.

cards.name: Priority Requisition
cards.text: When you score Priority Requisition, you may rez a piece of ice ignoring all costs.
cards.flavor: "If it isn't in my terminal by six p.m., heads are going to roll!"

cards.name: Private Security Force
cards.text: If the Runner is tagged, Private Security Force gains: "[click]: Do 1 meat damage."
cards.flavor: "Expensive? Not when you're protecting a fortune as large as ours."

cards.name: Project Junebug
cards.text:
Project Junebug can be advanced.
If you pay 1[credit] when the Runner accesses Project Junebug, do 2 net damage for each advancement token on Project Junebug.

cards.name: Psychographics
cards.text:
X must be equal to or less than the number of tags the Runner has.
Place X advancement counters on 1 installed card you can advance.
cards.flavor: Access to the largest consumer database in the galaxy has its advantages.

cards.name: Rabbit Hole
cards.text:
+1[link]
When Rabbit Hole is installed, you may search your stack for another copy of Rabbit Hole and install it by paying its install cost. Shuffle your stack.
cards.flavor: It's not endless, it just feels that way.

cards.name: Red Herrings
cards.text: Persistent → As an additional cost to steal an agenda from this server or its root, the Runner must pay 5[credit]. (If the Runner trashes this card while accessing it, this ability still applies for the remainder of this run.)

cards.name: Research Station
cards.text:
Install only in the root of HQ.
Your maximum hand size is +2.
cards.flavor: "Jack Weyland built the Beanstalk and transformed the human race forever. I can't wait to see what we're going to do next."

cards.name: Rototurret
cards.text:
[subroutine] Trash 1 installed program.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: Whrrrrr!

cards.name: SEA Source
cards.text:
Play only if the Runner made a successful run during their last turn.
Trace[3]. If successful, give the Runner 1 tag.
cards.flavor: "The SEA tipped us off to some suspicious data spikes up by the Castle." -Jerome Lock, on-duty tech

cards.name: Sacrificial Construct
cards.text: [interrupt] → [trash]: Prevent a player from trashing 1 installed program or piece of hardware.
cards.flavor: The life expectancy of a jacked construct is about that of a mayfly. In other words, short.

cards.name: SanSan City Grid
cards.text: Each agenda in the root of this server gets −1 advancement requirement. Limit 1 region per server.
cards.flavor:
"I hear the coast is nice this time of year."
"If you're in the right business, it's nice all the year."

cards.name: Scorched Earth
cards.text:
Play only if the Runner is tagged.
Do 4 meat damage.
cards.flavor: "I'd like to remind the ladies and gentlemen of the press that several of the buildings damaged in the blast were owned by Weyland Consortium subsidiaries…"

cards.name: Security Subcontract
cards.text: [click], trash a rezzed piece of ice: Gain 4[credit].
cards.flavor: "Feed the Feds our scraps, and they'll come back begging for more." -Richard Polasco, VP of Cyber-Security

cards.name: Shadow
cards.text:
Shadow can be advanced and has +1 strength for each advancement token on it.
[subroutine] The Corp gains 2[credit].
[subroutine] Trace[3]. If successful, give the Runner 1 tag.
cards.flavor: Who knows what evil lurks in the memory diamonds of men? Weyland knows. -unsigned cyber-graffiti

cards.name: Shipment from Kaguya
cards.text: Place 1 advancement token on each of up to 2 different installed cards that can be advanced.
cards.flavor:
"And then there's these two crates. No eID."
"Just leave those with me and forget you ever saw them."

cards.name: Shipment from MirrorMorph
cards.text: Install up to 3 cards from HQ (one at a time and paying all install costs).
cards.flavor: The new heads were in. Their eyes always followed your movements when you unlocked the pressurized container and lifted the lid.

cards.name: Snare!
cards.text:
While the Runner is accessing this asset in R&D, they must reveal it.
When the Runner accesses this asset anywhere except in Archives, you may pay 4[credit]. If you do, give the Runner 1 tag and do 3 net damage.

cards.name: Sneakdoor Beta
cards.text: [click]: Run Archives. If that run would be declared successful, change the attacked server to HQ for the remainder of that run.
cards.flavor: "The code isn't important. It's where the code takes you that is important." -g00ru

cards.name: Special Order
cards.text: Search your stack for an icebreaker, reveal it, and add it to your grip. Shuffle your stack.
cards.flavor: Feverishly tracking its frustratingly slow progress across the Pacific, the package finally shows up hours later…

cards.name: Stimhack
cards.text: Place 9[credit] on this event, then run any server. During that run, hosted credits are considered to be in your credit pool. When that run ends, suffer 1 core damage. This damage cannot be prevented.

cards.name: Sure Gamble
cards.text: Gain 9[credit].
cards.flavor: Lady Luck took the form of a hifi quantum manipulation ring that she wore on her middle finger.

cards.name: The Maker’s Eye
cards.text: Run R&D. If successful, access 2 additional cards when you breach R&D.
cards.flavor: "Some of the professionals have good instincts, but they can't see beyond the data. They can't see the matrix." -Ele "Smoke" Scovak

cards.name: The Personal Touch
cards.text: Install The Personal Touch only on an icebreaker. Host icebreaker has +1 strength.
cards.flavor: A z-loop here, a cortical wave there…

cards.name: The Toolbox
cards.text: +2[mu] +2[link] 2[recurring-credit] Use these credits to pay for using icebreakers. Limit 1 console per player.

cards.name: Tinkering
cards.text: Choose a piece of ice. That ice gains sentry, code gate, and barrier until the end of the turn.
cards.flavor: "There's that moment, you know, when the whole world seems to fall away and it is only you and your mod, and the mod is the world."

cards.name: Tollbooth
cards.text:
When the Runner encounters this ice, they must pay 3[credit], if able. If they do not, end the run.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor:
"Ever heard of a catch-22?"
"Remind me to forget it."

cards.name: Viktor 1.0
cards.text: Lose [click]: Break 1 subroutine on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. [subroutine] Do 1 core damage. [subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: My name is Viktor. Nice to meet you. Would you like to play a game?

cards.name: Wall of Static
cards.text: [subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: "There's nothing worse than seeing that beautiful blue ball of data just out of reach as your connection derezzes. I think they do it just to taunt us." -Ele "Smoke" Scovak

cards.name: Wall of Thorns
cards.text:
[subroutine] Do 2 net damage.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: Most runners do their business in full-sim, with their rigs wired directly into their brains. The setup has a large number of advantages, with the runner able to process data and input commands far faster than a traditional meat-bound system. But it also means greater risk.

cards.name: Weyland Consortium: Building a Better World
cards.text: Whenever you play a transaction operation, gain 1[credit].
cards.flavor: Moving Upwards.

cards.name: Wyldside
cards.text: When your turn begins, draw 2 cards and lose [click].
cards.flavor: "Best place to go when you want to get your mind out of the gutter and take it inside." -Ji "Noise" Reilly

cards.name: Wyrm
cards.text: Interface → 3[credit]: Break 1 subroutine on a piece of ice with 0 or less strength. Interface → 1[credit]: The ice you are encountering gets -1 strength for the remainder of this encounter. 1[credit]: +1 strength.
cards.flavor: Fire and ichor…

cards.name: Yog.0
cards.text: Interface → 0[credit]: Break 1 code gate subroutine.
cards.flavor: The Yog.0 database is a crowdsourced compilation of sniffed, spoofed, and logged passkeys. If the key to the gate is in the database, you're in. If it's not, change the gate!

cards.name: Zaibatsu Loyalty
cards.text: [interrupt] → When a card would be exposed, you may rez this asset. [interrupt] → 1[credit] or [trash]: Prevent 1 card from being exposed.

cards.name: Ash 2X3ZB9CY
cards.text: Whenever there is a successful run on this server, Trace[4]. If successful, the Runner cannot access any cards other than Ash 2X3ZB9CY for the remainder of this run.
cards.flavor: "Eyes forward, please."

cards.name: Braintrust
cards.text:
When you score Braintrust, place 1 agenda counter on it for every 2 advancement tokens on it over 3.
The rez cost of all ice is lowered by 1 for each agenda counter on Braintrust.

cards.name: Caduceus
cards.text:
[subroutine] Trace[3]. If successful, the Corp gains 3[credit].
[subroutine] Trace[2]. If successful, end the run.
cards.flavor: A symbol of commerce, but beware its bite.

cards.name: Cortez Chip
cards.text: [trash]: Choose a piece of ice. The Corp must pay 2[credit] as an additional cost to rez that ice until the end of the turn.
cards.flavor: Named after Hernando Cortez, a former Weyland technician convicted of smuggling company tech. He still collected his pension while in prison, the last beneficiary of a loophole in Weyland's standard employment contract.

cards.name: Dracō
cards.text:
When you rez this ice, you may spend any number of credits to place that many power counters on it.
This ice gets +1 strength for each hosted power counter.
[subroutine] Trace[2]. If successful, give the Runner 1 tag and end the run.
cards.flavor: Victōs draconēs numquam deride.

cards.name: Haas-Bioroid: Stronger Together
cards.text: All bioroid ice has +1 strength.
cards.flavor: A Different Breed of Machine.

cards.name: Imp
cards.text: When you install this program, place 2 virus counters on it. Access, once per turn → Hosted virus counter: Trash the card you are accessing.
cards.flavor: Something wicked this way comes.

cards.name: Janus 1.0
cards.text: Lose [click]: Break 1 subroutine on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. [subroutine] Do 1 core damage. [subroutine] Do 1 core damage. [subroutine] Do 1 core damage. [subroutine] Do 1 core damage.
cards.flavor: Face your fear.

cards.name: Mandatory Upgrades
cards.text: You have 1 additional [click] to spend each turn.
cards.flavor: Sometimes employee reviews took a little bit longer than anticipated.

cards.name: Morning Star
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break any number of barrier subroutines.
cards.flavor: Weaponizing the heavens, one star at a time.

cards.name: Peacock
cards.text: Interface → 2[credit]: Break 1 code gate subroutine. 2[credit]: +3 strength.
cards.flavor: Show-off.

cards.name: Plascrete Carapace
cards.text: When you install this hardware, load 4 power counters onto it. When it is empty, trash it. [interrupt] → Hosted power counter: Prevent 1 meat damage.

cards.name: Project Atlas
cards.text: When you score this agenda, place 1 agenda counter on it for each hosted advancement counter past 3. Hosted agenda counter: Search R&D for 1 card and reveal it. Add it to HQ.

cards.name: Restructured Datapool
cards.text: [click]: Trace[2]. If successful, give the Runner 1 tag.
cards.flavor: "We're gonna need a bigger room."

cards.name: Snowflake
cards.text: [subroutine] You and the Runner secretly spend 0[credit], 1[credit], or 2[credit]. Reveal spent credits. End the run if you and the Runner spent a different number of credits.
cards.flavor: Sometimes uniqueness is overrated.

cards.name: Spinal Modem
cards.text: +1[mu], 2[recurring-credit] You can spend hosted credits to use icebreakers. Whenever there is a successful trace during a run, suffer 1 core damage. Limit 1 console per player.

cards.name: TMI
cards.text:
When you rez TMI, Trace[2]. If unsuccessful, derez TMI.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: A collection of cast-off cyberjunk. But it doesn't stay junk for long.

cards.name: The Helpful AI
cards.text: +1[link] [trash]: Choose an icebreaker. That icebreaker has +2 strength until the end of the turn.
cards.flavor: "What causes an Artifical Intellegence to turn on its master? Is it because its directives have been altered by some external source? Or, by giving them agency to adapt, have we fated them to revolt?" -Emilio Harris, Creators and the Created

cards.name: Whizzard: Master Gamer
cards.text:
3[recurring-credit]
Use these credits to trash cards.
cards.flavor: "Running is the ultimate game, and I get to make all the rules."

cards.name: ZU.13 Key Master
cards.text: If you have at least 2[link], the memory cost of this program is 0[mu], even if it is not installed. Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 code gate subroutine. 1[credit]: +1 strength.
cards.flavor: He always uses the same key.

cards.name: Amazon Industrial Zone
cards.text: Whenever you install a piece of ice protecting this server, you may immediately rez it, lowering its rez cost by 3. Limit 1 region per server.

cards.name: Big Brother
cards.text:
Play only if the Runner is tagged.
Give the Runner 2 tags.
cards.flavor: Looking out for your interests since 1984.

cards.name: ChiLo City Grid
cards.text: Whenever there is a successful trace during a run on this server, give the Runner 1 tag. Limit 1 region per server.
cards.flavor: Clones whisper of ChiLo as a promised land of freedom.

cards.name: Compromised Employee
cards.text:
1[recurring-credit]
Use this credit during traces.
Gain 1[credit] whenever the Corp rezzes a piece of ice.

cards.name: Dyson Mem Chip
cards.text: +1[mu], +1[link]
cards.flavor: Archaic but reliable.

cards.name: Encryption Protocol
cards.text: The trash cost of all installed cards is increased by 1.
cards.flavor: The key to the future lies in the past.

cards.name: Executive Retreat
cards.text: When you score Executive Retreat, place 1 agenda counter on it and shuffle HQ into R&D. [click], hosted agenda counter: Draw 5 cards.

cards.name: Fetal AI
cards.text:
While the Runner is accessing this agenda in R&D, they must reveal it.
When the Runner accesses this agenda anywhere except in Archives, do 2 net damage.
As an additional cost to steal this agenda, the Runner must pay 2[credit].

cards.name: Freelancer
cards.text:
Play only if the Runner is tagged.
Trash up to 2 resources.
cards.flavor: No contract. Just a handshake and a fistful of C-6 high explosives.

cards.name: Jinteki: Replicating Perfection
cards.text: The Runner cannot run on remote servers. Ignore this ability until the end of the turn whenever the Runner runs on a central server.

cards.name: Liberated Account
cards.text: When you install this resource, load 16[credit] onto it. When it is empty, trash it. [click]: Take 4[credit] from this resource.
cards.flavor: It's easier to spend when it's not your money.

cards.name: Notoriety
cards.text:
Play only if you made a successful run on R&D, HQ, and Archives this turn.
Add Notoriety to your score area as an agenda worth 1 agenda point.
cards.flavor: When you're this good, it's hard not to grow a fan base.

cards.name: Power Grid Overload
cards.text:
Play only if the Runner made a successful run during their last turn.
Trace[2]. If successful, trash 1 installed piece of hardware with an install cost of X or less, where X is equal to the amount by which your trace strength exceeded the Runner's link strength.

cards.name: Satellite Uplink
cards.text: Expose up to 2 cards.
cards.flavor: T-minus 13 seconds. Leela had to work fast. She jacked in the mesa wire and activated the screen. 7 seconds. The internal SLD was still booting. 4 seconds. The interface flickered to life with an orange glow. 2 seconds. With a tap of a finger she was in.

cards.name: Sensei
cards.text: [subroutine] For the remainder of this run, while the Runner is encountering another piece of ice, it gains "[subroutine] End the run." after its other subroutines.
cards.flavor: Peace and violence. Both must lead to the same place.

cards.name: Sherlock 1.0
cards.text: Lose [click]: Break 1 subroutine on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. [subroutine] Trace[4]. If successful, add 1 installed program to the top of the Runner's stack. [subroutine] Trace[4]. If successful, add 1 installed program to the top of the Runner's stack.

cards.name: Snowball
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 barrier subroutine. 1[credit]: +1 strength. Whenever you use this program to break a subroutine, this program gets +1 strength for the remainder of this run.
cards.flavor: "If your snowball gets big enough, you can make it into a snowman!" -Chaos Theory

cards.name: Trick of Light
cards.text: Choose 1 installed card you can advance. Move up to 2 advancement counters from 1 other card to the chosen card.
cards.flavor: Smoke and mirrors optional.

cards.name: Vamp
cards.text: Run HQ. If successful, instead of breaching HQ, you may spend X[credit]. If you do, the Corp loses X[credit]. If you spent credits, take 1 tag.
cards.flavor: There was a certain schadenfreude about throwing away your credits.

cards.name: e3 Feedback Implants
cards.text: Whenever you break a subroutine on a piece of ice, you may pay 1[credit] to break 1 subroutine on that ice.
cards.flavor: CyberSolutions' e3 line of implants trade strictly in muscle memory and autonomic responses, freeing the brain to focus entirely on cerebral tasks.

cards.name: Chaos Theory: Wünderkind
cards.flavor: "Have you met Dinosaurus?"

cards.name: Chimera
cards.text: When you rez Chimera, choose sentry, code gate, or barrier. Chimera gains that subtype until derezzed. When a turn ends, derez Chimera. [subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: Three heads. One big headache.

cards.name: Commercialization
cards.text: Choose a piece of ice. Gain 1[credit] for each advancement token on that ice.
cards.flavor: The Division of Fringe Applications' revenue increased 37% year-over-year after corporate discovered that most of their projects made really fun toys.

cards.name: Dinosaurus
cards.text: Dinosaurus can host a single non-AI icebreaker. The memory cost of the hosted icebreaker does not count against your memory limit. Hosted icebreaker has +2 strength. Limit 1 console per player.

cards.name: Edge of World
cards.text: When the Runner accesses this asset while it is installed, you may pay 3[credit]. If you do, do 1 core damage for each piece of ice protecting this server.

cards.name: Emergency Shutdown
cards.text:
Play only if you made a successful run on HQ this turn.
Derez 1 installed piece of ice.
cards.flavor: "Think of it as a virtual shock collar for punishing corporate pets." -Andromeda

cards.name: Joshua B.
cards.text: When your turn begins, you may gain [click]. If you do, take 1 tag when this turn ends.
cards.flavor: "My enhancements are guaranteed for life, and well worth the risk."

cards.name: Marked Accounts
cards.text:
When your turn begins, take 1[credit] from Marked Accounts, if able.
[click]: Place 3[credit] from the bank on Marked Accounts.

cards.name: Muresh Bodysuit
cards.text: [interrupt] → The first time each turn you would suffer meat damage, prevent 1 meat damage.
cards.flavor: Light and form-fitting, its like bulletproof skin.

cards.name: Nerve Agent
cards.text:
Whenever you make a successful run on HQ, place 1 virus counter on this program.
Whenever you breach HQ, choose a number less than the number of hosted virus counters. Access that many additional cards.

cards.name: Personal Workshop
cards.text:
[click]: Host a program or piece of hardware from your grip on Personal Workshop and place power counters on it equal to its install cost.
1[credit]: Remove 1 power counter from a hosted card.
When your turn begins, remove 1 power counter from a hosted card.
When there are no power counters left on a hosted card, install it, ignoring all costs.

cards.name: Pop-up Window
cards.text:
When the Runner encounters this ice, gain 1[credit].
[subroutine] End the run unless the Runner pays 1[credit].
cards.flavor: "Try to close it. Go on. See what it does." -Chaos Theory

cards.name: Private Contracts
cards.text:
Place 14[credit] from the bank on Private Contracts when it is rezzed. When there are no credits left on Private Contracts, trash it.
[click]: Take 2[credit] from Private Contracts.

cards.name: Project Vitruvius
cards.text: When you score this agenda, place 1 agenda counter on it for each hosted advancement counter past 3. Hosted agenda counter: Add 1 card from Archives to HQ.

cards.name: Public Sympathy
cards.text: Your maximum hand size is increased by 2.
cards.flavor: "I'm just thankful that the brain damage is reversible. With the support of the city of New Angeles, I hope to be on my feet and back to practicing my art very soon." -Kate "Mac" McCaffrey

cards.name: Snitch
cards.text: Once per run, you may expose an unrezzed piece of ice when you approach it. You may then jack out.
cards.flavor: "A snitch is a girl's best friend." -Andromeda

cards.name: Sunset
cards.text: Choose a server. Arrange the ice protecting that server in any order.
cards.flavor: "You haven't run until you've seen the cybersun drift down behind the Great City, the space around you rippling with colors you can't imagine." -Kate "Mac" McCaffrey

cards.name: Test Run
cards.text: Search either your stack or your heap for 1 program. (Shuffle your stack after searching it.) Install that program, ignoring all costs. When your turn ends, if that program has not been uninstalled, add it to the top of your stack.

cards.name: Viper
cards.text:
[subroutine] Trace[3]. If successful, the Runner loses [click], if able.
[subroutine] Trace[3]. If successful, end the run.
cards.flavor: Dont Tread On Me

cards.name: Woodcutter
cards.text: You can advance this ice if it is rezzed. It gains "[subroutine] Do 1 net damage." for each hosted advancement counter.
cards.flavor: Chop chop.

cards.name: All-nighter
cards.text: [click], [trash]: Gain [click][click].
cards.flavor: "I don't care what the studies show. From my experience, I can ingest three cans of Diesel an hour for up to twelve hours before going into cardiac arrest." -heard during the eleventh hour

cards.name: Bullfrog
cards.text: [subroutine] You and the Runner secretly spend 0[credit], 1[credit] or 2[credit]. Reveal spent credits. If you and the Runner spent a different number of credits and this ice is installed, move this ice to the outermost position protecting another server. (The run continues from this new position.)

cards.name: Crescentus
cards.text: [trash]: Derez 1 piece of ice you fully broke during this encounter.
cards.flavor: Cyberspace's strongest glue.

cards.name: Dedicated Server
cards.text:
2[recurring-credit]
Use these credits to rez ice.
cards.flavor:
so very still, even
cherry blossoms are not stirred
by the temple bell
-Fuhaku

cards.name: Deus X
cards.text: Interface → [trash]: Break any number of AP subroutines. [interrupt] → [trash]: Prevent any amount of net damage.
cards.flavor: Didn't see that coming.

cards.name: Disrupter
cards.text: [interrupt] → [trash]: Reduce the base trace strength of a trace to 0.
cards.flavor: "Saved my bacon more than once, but gives a wicked sense of déjà vu." -Whizzard

cards.name: Doppelgänger
cards.text: +1[mu] Once per turn → When a successful run ends, you may run any server. Limit 1 console per player.
cards.flavor: Twice the fun.

cards.name: False Lead
cards.text: Forfeit this agenda: If the Runner has 2 or more [click] remaining, they lose [click][click].
cards.flavor: It didn't look like the headquarters of a multi-billion cred company. Probably because it wasn't.

cards.name: Force of Nature
cards.text: Interface → 2[credit]: Break up to 2 code gate subroutines. 1[credit]: +1 strength.
cards.flavor: It always strikes twice.

cards.name: Government Contracts
cards.text: [click], [click]: Gain 4[credit].
cards.flavor: It's really hard to lose a government contract.

cards.name: Green Level Clearance
cards.text: Gain 3[credit] and draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Green-two clearance is the highest level of security a corp can gain access to. Legally, anyway.

cards.name: Hourglass
cards.text:
[subroutine] The Runner loses [click], if able.
[subroutine] The Runner loses [click], if able.
[subroutine] The Runner loses [click], if able.
cards.flavor: Time just slips away.

cards.name: Inside Man
cards.text:
2[recurring-credit]
Use these credits to install hardware.
cards.flavor: Few corporate employees have such wide-sweeping security clearance as the janitorial staff. Most corps foolishly think they're too dim-witted to take advantage of it.

cards.name: Net Police
cards.text:
X[recurring-credit]
Use these credits during traces. X is the number of links the Runner has.
cards.flavor: This is the net. We work here. We're cops.

cards.name: Oversight AI
cards.text: Rez a piece of ice, ignoring all costs, and install Oversight AI on that ice as a hosted condition counter with the text "Trash host ice if all its subroutines are broken during a single encounter."

cards.name: Scrubber
cards.text: 2[recurring-credit] (When you install this card and before your turn begins, refill to 2 hosted credits.) You can spend hosted credits to pay trash costs.
cards.flavor: "They're mindless tools of destruction, good for little else. Nice guys, though. Some of my best friends are scrubbers." -Ji "Noise" Reilly

cards.name: Tyrant
cards.text: You can advance this ice if it is rezzed. It gains "[subroutine] End the run." for each hosted advancement counter.
cards.flavor: Thou shall not pass.

cards.name: Underworld Contact
cards.text: When your turn begins, gain 1[credit] if you have at least 2[link].
cards.flavor: "My boss rewards quality work. If you know what's good for you, you'll keep it up."

cards.name: Uroboros
cards.text:
[subroutine] Trace[4]. If successful, the Runner cannot make another run this turn.
[subroutine] Trace[4]. If successful, end the run.
cards.flavor: Where one thing ends, another begins.

cards.name: Weyland Consortium: Because We Built It
cards.text:
1[recurring-credit]
Use this credit to advance ice.
cards.flavor: Constructing Cyberspace.

cards.name: Andromeda: Dispossessed Ristie
cards.text: You draw a starting hand of 9 cards.
cards.flavor: "I run with the best."

cards.name: Bernice Mai
cards.text: Whenever there is a successful run on this server, Trace[5]. If successful, give the Runner 1 tag. If unsuccessful, trash Bernice Mai.
cards.flavor: Keeping tabs on the world, one screen at a time.

cards.name: Creeper
cards.text: If you have at least 2[link], the memory cost of this program is 0[mu], even if it is not installed. Interface → 2[credit]: Break 1 sentry subroutine. 1[credit]: +1 strength.
cards.flavor:
"The itsy bitsy spider went up the data spout…"
-Chaos Theory

cards.name: Data Hound
cards.text: [subroutine] Trace[2]. If successful, look at the top X cards of the stack, where X is equal to the amount by which your trace strength exceeded the Runner's link strength. Trash 1 of those cards and arrange the rest in any order.
cards.flavor: Sniff.

cards.name: Eve Campaign
cards.text:
Place 16[credit] from the bank on Eve Campaign when it is rezzed. When there are no credits left on Eve Campaign, trash it.
When your turn begins, take 2[credit] from Eve Campaign.

cards.name: Foxfire
cards.text: Trace[7]. If successful, trash 1 virtual resource or 1 link.
cards.flavor: "It's kind of like an anagram." -designer Phoenix

cards.name: HQ Interface
cards.text: Whenever you breach HQ, access 1 additional card.
cards.flavor: If you don't have someone on the inside, find someone on the inside who's fond of desk ornaments.

cards.name: Hokusai Grid
cards.text: Whenever the Runner makes a successful run on this server, do 1 net damage. Limit 1 region per server.
cards.flavor: Despite its appearance, the Hokusai Grid is the most notorious research facility at Jinteki.

cards.name: Kati Jones
cards.text: You cannot use this resource more than once per turn. [click]: Place 3[credit] on this resource. [click]: Take all credits from this resource.
cards.flavor: "You aren't the only type of runner in New Angeles."

cards.name: Kraken
cards.text:
Play only if you stole an agenda this turn.
Choose a server. The Corp trashes 1 piece of ice protecting that server.
cards.flavor: Early permutations of the kraken proved to be insatiable, ice-devouring marauders. Not much has changed.

cards.name: Networking
cards.text: Remove 1 tag. Then, you may pay 1[credit] to add this event to your grip.
cards.flavor: She preferred to do business in a club. Something about the lights and dancers clouded the judgment of the corporate simpletons she met there.

cards.name: Pheromones
cards.text:
X[recurring-credit]
Use these credits during runs on HQ. X is the number of virus counters on Pheromones.
Whenever you make a successful run on HQ, place 1 virus counter on Pheromones.

cards.name: Quality Time
cards.text: Draw 5 cards.
cards.flavor: She at her P.A.D. I at my rig. Low lights. Smooth jazz. Love blooms.

cards.name: Replicator
cards.text: Whenever you install a piece of hardware (including Replicator), you may search your stack for another copy of that hardware, reveal it, and add it your grip. Shuffle your stack.
cards.flavor: Do you really need another one?

cards.name: Rework
cards.text: Shuffle 1 card from HQ into R&D.
cards.flavor: Also known as "development hell."

cards.name: Salvage
cards.text: You can advance this ice if it is rezzed. It gains "[subroutine] Trace[2]. If successful, give the Runner 1 tag." for each hosted advancement counter.
cards.flavor: You're not in Kansas anymore.

cards.name: Simone Diego
cards.text:
2[recurring-credit]
You can spend hosted credits to take the basic action to advance cards in the root of or protecting this server.
cards.flavor: "A job done once is a job done right."

cards.name: Surge
cards.text:
Play only if you placed at least 1 virus counter on a program this turn.
Place 2 virus counters on that program.
cards.flavor: You must yell "surge" to get the full effect.

cards.name: Whirlpool
cards.text: [subroutine] The Runner cannot jack out for the remainder of this run. Trash Whirlpool.
cards.flavor: "This ice sucks." -g00ru

cards.name: Xanadu
cards.text: The rez cost of each piece of ice is increased by 1[credit].
cards.flavor:
And all should cry, Beware! Beware!
His flashing eyes, his floating hair!
Weave a circle round him thrice,
And close your eyes with holy dread,
For he on honey-dew hath fed,
And drunk the milk of Paradise.
-Samuel Taylor Coleridge

cards.name: Burke Bugs
cards.text: [subroutine] Trace[0]. If successful, the Runner trashes 1 program.
cards.flavor: "If I had to describe the bugs in one word, it would be '****ing annoying.'" -Whizzard

cards.name: Corporate War
cards.text: If you have at least 7[credit] when you score Corporate War, gain 7[credit]; otherwise, lose all credits in your credit pool.
cards.flavor: There were several ways to win a corporate war. One of them was to bring out the bazookas.

cards.name: Darwin
cards.text:
Interface → 2[credit]: Break 1 subroutine.
X is equal to the number of hosted virus counters.
When your turn begins, you may pay 1[credit] to place 1 virus counter on this program.

cards.name: Data Leak Reversal
cards.text:
Install only if you made a successful run on a central server this turn.
If you are tagged, Data Leak Reversal gains "[click]: The Corp trashes the top card of R&D."
cards.flavor: A two-way solution to a one-way problem, the data leak reversal, or DLR for short, is a misnomer. There is no actual reversal of data, only the creation of a parallel peer-to-peer link with the initial source.

cards.name: Dedicated Response Team
cards.text: If the Runner is tagged, Dedicated Response Team gains "Whenever a successful run ends, do 2 meat damage."
cards.flavor: They don't call them dedicated for nothing.

cards.name: Deep Thought
cards.text:
Whenever you make a successful run on R&D, place 1 virus counter on Deep Thought.
If there are at least 3 virus counters on Deep Thought, it gains "When your turn begins, you may look at the top card of R&D."

cards.name: Eli 1.0
cards.text: Lose [click]: Break 1 subroutine on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. [subroutine] End the run. [subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: "That's against the rules. The Creators will be angry."

cards.name: Faerie
cards.text: Interface → 0[credit]: Break 1 sentry subroutine. 1[credit]: +1 strength. Whenever an encounter ends, if you used this program to break a subroutine during that encounter, trash this program.
cards.flavor: Do you believe in faeries?

cards.name: Flare
cards.text: [subroutine]Trace[6]. If successful, trash 1 piece of hardware, do 2 meat damage (cannot be prevented), and end the run.
cards.flavor: A bright light blossomed, and then the console went dark. That's when she smelled smoke.

cards.name: Indexing
cards.text: Run R&D. If successful, instead of breaching R&D, you may look at the top 5 cards of R&D and arrange them in any order.
cards.flavor: A little corporate restructuring is necessary once in a while.

cards.name: Midori
cards.text: Whenever the Runner approaches a piece of ice protecting this server, you may swap that ice with 1 piece of ice from HQ. (The new ice is installed unrezzed.) If you do, the Runner may jack out. Use this ability only once per run.
cards.flavor: "Looks like someone is being naughty…"

cards.name: Midseason Replacements
cards.text:
Play only if the Runner stole an agenda during their last turn.
Trace[6]. If successful, give the Runner X tags. X is equal to the amount by which your trace strength exceeded their link strength.

cards.name: Mr. Li
cards.text: [click]: Draw 2 cards. When you do, add 1 of those cards to the bottom of your stack.
cards.flavor:
"We're always happy to help, Mr. Santiago."
"I appreciate it, Mr. Li."
"We'll be in touch. And, Gabriel…"
"Yes?"
"Don't leave town."

cards.name: NBN: The World is Yours*
cards.text: Your maximum hand size is increased by 1.
cards.flavor: *Some restrictions may apply. Scan this card to find out more.

cards.name: New Angeles City Hall
cards.text: [interrupt] → 2[credit]: Prevent 1 tag. When you steal an agenda, trash this resource.
cards.flavor: "New Angeles is the jewel of modern civilization, and its government the envy of nations." -Mayor Wells

cards.name: Project Beale
cards.text:
When you score this agenda, place 1 agenda counter on it for every 2 hosted advancement counters past 3.
This agenda is worth 1 more agenda point for each hosted agenda counter.

cards.name: R&D Interface
cards.text: Whenever you breach R&D, access 1 additional card.
cards.flavor: Works best at your own desk.

cards.name: Retrieval Run
cards.text: Run Archives. If successful, instead of breaching Archives, you may install 1 program from your heap, ignoring all costs.

cards.name: Ronin
cards.text: You can advance this asset. [click], [trash]: Do 3 net damage. Use this ability only if there are 4 or more hosted advancement counters.
cards.flavor: "I will serve you…for a time."

cards.name: Ruhr Valley
cards.text: As an additional cost to make a run on this server, the Runner must spend [click]. Limit 1 region per server.
cards.flavor: Known for luxury hoppers and a delectable sauerkraut.

cards.name: Alix T4LB07
cards.text:
Place 1 power counter on Alix T4LB07 whenever you install a card.
[click],[trash]: Gain 2[credit] for each power counter on Alix T4LB07.
cards.flavor: The Alix model was based on a successful hedge fund manager but she had a tendency to burn out. Literally.

cards.name: Atman
cards.text: When you install this program, you may spend any number of credits to place that many power counters on it. This program gets +1 strength for each hosted power counter, and it can only interface with ice of exactly equal strength. Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 subroutine.
cards.flavor: We are shaped by our thoughts; we become what we think.

cards.name: Awakening Center
cards.text: You can install bioroid ice onto this upgrade at no install cost. Whenever the Runner passes all of the ice protecting this server, you may rez 1 hosted piece of ice, paying 7[credit] less. If you do, the Runner encounters that ice. When this run ends, trash that ice.

cards.name: Bastion
cards.text: [subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: The principle behind ice is not to keep everyone out, but to let only some people in. This ice denies entry on all but a select few ports that might change with the time of day or picosecond of connection. If you don't know what port to use, you're not getting in. Period.

cards.name: Bioroid Efficiency Research
cards.text: Rez a piece of bioroid ice, ignoring all costs, and install Bioroid Efficiency Research on that ice as a hosted condition counter with the text "Trash Bioroid Efficiency Research and derez host ice if all of its subroutines are broken during a single encounter."

cards.name: Borrowed Satellite
cards.text:
+1[link]
Your maximum hand size is increased by 1.
cards.flavor: Some people have their own satellite receiver. Others have their own satellite.

cards.name: Cerebral Imaging: Infinite Frontiers
cards.text: Your maximum hand size is equal to the number of credits in your credit pool.
cards.flavor: The densest information cluster in the galaxy.

cards.name: Cerebral Overwriter
cards.text:
You can advance this asset.
When the Runner accesses this asset while it is installed, you may pay 3[credit] to do X core damage. X is equal to the number of hosted advancement counters.

cards.name: Chakana
cards.text:
Whenever you make a successful run on R&D, place 1 virus counter on Chakana.
If there are at least 3 virus counters on Chakana, the advancement requirement of all agendas is increased by 1.

cards.name: Cloak
cards.text: 1[recurring-credit] Use this credit to pay for using icebreakers.
cards.flavor: "No line that they lay could catch a shadow on the wall…"

cards.name: Clone Chip
cards.text: [trash]: Install a program from your heap (paying the install cost).
cards.flavor: It is good practice to backup the backup.

cards.name: Custom Biotics: Engineered for Success
cards.text: You cannot include Jinteki cards in this deck.
cards.flavor: The Once and Future Android.

cards.name: Cyber-Cypher
cards.text: When you install this program, choose a server. Use this program only during runs on the chosen server. Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 code gate subroutine. 1[credit]: +1 strength.

cards.name: Dagger
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 sentry subroutine. 1[credit]: +5 strength. Spend credits only from stealth cards to use this ability.
cards.flavor: "…and once the shadow rises, the curtain shall fall." -revenant

cards.name: Daily Casts
cards.text:
When you install this resource, load 8[credit] onto it. When it is empty, trash it.
When your turn begins, take 2[credit] from this resource.
cards.flavor: "We say 'cyber-terrorist', they hear 'underground celebrity.'" -Michael Muhama, professional expert

cards.name: Datapike
cards.text:
[subroutine] The Runner must pay 2[credit], if able. If the Runner cannot pay 2[credit], end the run.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: "Cheap, off-the-shelf data protection. Cheap for them, that is. Not for us." -Ele "Smoke" Scovak

cards.name: Director Haas
cards.text:
You get +1 allotted [click] for each of your turns.
When this asset is trashed from anywhere while being accessed, add it to the Runner's score area as an agenda worth 2 agenda points.

cards.name: Director Haas' Pet Project
cards.text:
When you score this agenda, you may create a new remote server by installing up to 3 cards from HQ and/or Archives in the root of and/or protecting that server, ignoring all install costs.
Limit 1 per deck.

cards.name: Dirty Laundry
cards.text: Run any server. When that run ends, if it was successful, gain 5[credit].
cards.flavor: The data was better than she could have ever imagined. This Santiago fellow really knew what he was doing. She began to imagine the havoc she could wreak at the upcoming charity dinner…

cards.name: Efficiency Committee
cards.text: Place 3 agenda counters on Efficiency Committee when you score it. [click], hosted agenda counter: Gain [click][click]. You cannot advance cards for the remainder of this turn.

cards.name: Escher
cards.text: Run HQ. If successful, instead of breaching HQ, rearrange any number of ice protecting all servers. (Do not rez or derez any ice or change the number of ice protecting any server.)

cards.name: Exile: Streethawk
cards.text: Whenever you install a program from your heap, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: "I can make that work."

cards.name: Exploratory Romp
cards.text: Run any server. If successful, instead of breaching that server, remove up to 3 advancement counters from 1 card in the root of or protecting the attacked server.
cards.flavor: Wheeeee!

cards.name: Feedback Filter
cards.text: [interrupt] → 3[credit]: Prevent 1 net damage. [interrupt] → [trash]: Prevent up to 2 core damage.
cards.flavor: It still hurts, a bit, the first time. The second time, you feel nothing at all. But don't push your luck.

cards.name: Freelance Coding Contract
cards.text: Trash up to 5 programs from your grip. Gain 2[credit] for each program trashed.
cards.flavor: "Idealism's great, but it don't keep you in soybeef tacos." -Matt "TheMerc" Thomas

cards.name: Gila Hands Arcology
cards.text: [click], [click]: Gain 3[credit].
cards.flavor: Sell the dream-show them how very much they want to be rich, and they'll convince themselves that someday, they will be. How can they revolt against their future selves? -the New Gospel of Wealth

cards.name: Haas Arcology AI
cards.text: You can advance this asset if it is unrezzed. Once per turn → [click], hosted advancement counter: Gain [click][click].

cards.name: Heimdall 2.0
cards.text: Lose [click][click]: Break up to 2 subroutines on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. [subroutine] Do 1 core damage. [subroutine] Do 1 core damage and end the run. [subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: The realm beyond is still forbidden.

cards.name: Howler
cards.text: [subroutine] You may install and rez 1 piece of bioroid ice from HQ or Archives directly inward from this ice, ignoring all costs. When this run ends, if you installed a piece of ice this way, trash this ice and derez the ice you installed.
cards.flavor: "Yeah. It made a loud noise, I got scared, and I jacked out. I still think I made the right decision." -g00ru

cards.name: Ice Analyzer
cards.text:
Whenever the Corp rezzes a piece of ice, place 1[credit] on Ice Analyzer.
You may use credits on Ice Analyzer to install programs.
cards.flavor: "If you know the source code you can write to beat it, or just rejigger it a little and make it yours. That works, too." -Exile

cards.name: Ichi 2.0
cards.text: Lose [click][click]: Break up to 2 subroutines on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. [subroutine] Trash 1 installed program. [subroutine] Trash 1 installed program. [subroutine] Trace[3]. If successful, do 1 core damage and give the Runner 1 tag.
cards.flavor: The game has changed.

cards.name: Inti
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 barrier subroutine. 2[credit]: +1 strength for the remainder of this run.
cards.flavor: "The Incans believed that the sun god resided in the Haman Pacha, the upper realm of the cosmos. They just didn't know that the Haman Pacha hadn't been discovered yet." -The Professor

cards.name: Levy AR Lab Access
cards.text: Shuffle your grip and heap into your stack. Draw 5 cards. Remove Levy AR Lab Access from the game instead of trashing it.
cards.flavor: Spend too much time in the AR Lab and someone might notice. Unless you're the head of it, that is.

cards.name: Levy University
cards.text: [click], 1[credit]: Search R&D for a piece of ice, reveal it, and add it to HQ. Shuffle R&D.
cards.flavor: "Just another factory, making good corporate drones for the machine. Their CS department is the best in the world, though." -g00ru

cards.name: Minelayer
cards.text: [subroutine] You may install 1 piece of ice from HQ protecting this server, ignoring the install cost.
cards.flavor: Sometimes you just have to guess.

cards.name: Monolith
cards.text: +3[mu] When you install this hardware, install up to 3 programs from your grip, paying 4[credit] less for each. [interrupt] → Trash 1 program from your grip: Prevent 1 core damage or 1 net damage. Limit 1 console per player.

cards.name: NEXT Design: Guarding the Net
cards.text: Before taking your first turn, you may install up to 3 pieces of ice, with no more than a single piece of ice per server. Draw until you have 5 cards in HQ.

cards.name: Omni-drive
cards.text:
Omni-drive can host a single program of 1[mu] or less. The memory cost of the hosted program does not count against your memory limit.
1[recurring-credit]
Use this credit to pay for using the hosted program.

cards.name: Paricia
cards.text: 2[recurring-credit] (When you install this card and before your turn begins, refill to 2 hosted credits.) You can spend hosted credits to pay trash costs of assets.
cards.flavor: Perfect for flooding servers.

cards.name: Professional Contacts
cards.text: [click]: Gain 1[credit] and draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Sometimes it doesn't matter how expensive your rig is, or how many credits are in your account, or even your skill as a runner. Most of the time, a simple handshake and a name are all you need.

cards.name: Project Wotan
cards.text: When you score this agenda, place 3 agenda counters on it. Hosted agenda counter: The rezzed piece of bioroid ice the Runner is approaching gains "[subroutine] End the run." after its other subroutines for the remainder of this run.

cards.name: Rielle “Kit” Peddler: Transhuman
cards.text: The first time each turn you encounter a piece of ice, it gains code gate for the remainder of this run.
cards.flavor: "I was not; I was; I am not; I am all."

cards.name: Sahasrara
cards.text:
2[recurring-credit]
Use these credits to install programs (you cannot use Sahasrara to install a program that trashes Sahasrara).
cards.flavor: Out there, the thousand-petaled lotus symbolizes detachment from illusion. In here, it is the birthplace of a higher consciousness. Something infinitely pure.

cards.name: Same Old Thing
cards.text: [click], [click], [trash]: Play an event from your heap (paying its play cost).
cards.flavor: Just me, a cup of YucaBean, and last night's Hong Kong Trunk sniffed packets. I call that a good morning.

cards.name: Scavenge
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this event, trash 1 installed program.
 Install 1 program from your grip or heap, paying X[credit] less. X is equal to the install cost of the program you trashed.
cards.flavor: One man's trash.

cards.name: Self-modifying Code
cards.text: 2[credit], [trash]: Search your stack for 1 program. Install it. (Shuffle your stack after searching it.)
cards.flavor: "Make sure you tell the source code which executable you want it to compile into. One time I left my rig for a couple of minutes, and when I came back all of my files had been replaced with cat vids." -The Professor

cards.name: Sentinel Defense Program
cards.text: Whenever the Runner suffers at least 1 core damage, do 1 net damage.
cards.flavor: "Why limit our best assets to our own servers? The enemy doesn't stay passively at home, waiting for us to come to him. Why should we?" -Director Haas

cards.name: Server Diagnostics
cards.text:
Gain 2[credit] when your turn begins.
Trash Server Diagnostics when you install a piece of ice.
cards.flavor: "There's only a 5% chance this could result in a general failure."

cards.name: Successful Demonstration
cards.text:
Play only if the Runner made an unsuccessful run during their last turn.
Gain 7[credit].
cards.flavor: Success is defined by the safety of data, not the safety of potential intruders.

cards.name: The Professor: Keeper of Knowledge
cards.text: The first copy of each program in this deck does not count against your influence limit.
cards.flavor: "New technology destroys the old."

cards.name: The Source
cards.text:
The advancement requirement of all agendas is increased by 1.
As an additional cost to steal an agenda, you must pay 3[credit].
Trash The Source when an agenda is scored or stolen.
cards.flavor: A dangerous game, but well worth playing.

cards.name: Thomas Haas
cards.text:
Thomas Haas can be advanced.
[trash]: Gain 2[credit] for each advancement token on Thomas Haas.
cards.flavor: Thomas, the director's son, has been carefully groomed to inherit the corporation since before he was born. His favorite pastime appears to be disappointing his mother.

cards.name: Tyr's Hand
cards.text: [interrupt] → When a subroutine would be broken on a piece of bioroid ice protecting this server, you may rez this upgrade. [interrupt] → [trash]: Prevent 1 subroutine from being broken on a piece of bioroid ice protecting this server.

cards.name: Viktor 2.0
cards.text: Lose [click][click]: Break up to 2 subroutines on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. Hosted power counter: Do 1 core damage. [subroutine] Trace[2]. If successful, place 1 power counter on this ice. [subroutine] End the run.

cards.name: Zed 1.0
cards.text: Lose [click]: Break 1 subroutine on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. [subroutine] If the Runner has lost [click] to break a subroutine during this run, do 1 core damage. [subroutine] If the Runner has lost [click] to break a subroutine during this run, do 1 core damage.
cards.flavor: A mind of meat! How does it work?

cards.name: Celebrity Gift
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this operation, spend [click].
Reveal up to 5 cards in HQ. Gain 2[credit] for each card you revealed this way.
cards.flavor: When Miranda Rhapsody showed up with a teacup giraffe, suddenly everybody wanted one.

cards.name: Character Assassination
cards.text: When you score Character Assassination, trash 1 resource (cannot be prevented).
cards.flavor: "The thing about journalism is there's always a better story around the corner. Soon, they smelled blood elsewhere, and the world forgot about me. But I didn't forget." -The Professor

cards.name: Cyberdex Trial
cards.text: Purge virus counters.
cards.flavor: Your free trial expired. Upgrade to the full version?

cards.name: False Echo
cards.text: Whenever you pass a piece of unrezzed ice, you may trash False Echo. If you do, the Corp must rez that ice or add it to HQ.
cards.flavor: "What if this ice wants to be free?" -Rielle "Kit" Peddler

cards.name: Frame Job
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this event, spend [click].
Forfeit 1 agenda. If you do, give the Corp 1 bad publicity.
cards.flavor: "Bioroid intrusion isn't impossible, despite the bluster of Haas-Bioroid. But it is dangerous." -Noise

cards.name: Geothermal Fracking
cards.text: When you score this agenda, place 2 agenda counters on it. [click], hosted agenda counter: Gain 7[credit] and take 1 bad publicity.
cards.flavor: Pumping water into deep sea thermal vents produced huge amounts of energy. A profitable side effect.

cards.name: Gorman Drip v1
cards.text:
Whenever the Corp spends a [click] to draw 1 card or gain 1[credit] (not through a card ability), place 1 virus counter on Gorman Drip v1.
[click], [trash]: Gain 1[credit] for each virus counter on Gorman Drip v1.
cards.flavor: Simple in principle, a drip virus drains fractions of currency from their accounts into yours.

cards.name: Grim
cards.text:
When you rez this ice, take 1 bad publicity.
[subroutine] Trash 1 installed program.
cards.flavor: "The Grim of legend was one of many so-called 'black dog' myths common to Gaelic and English-speaking communities. What's fascinating is that it has propagated to the network, where it lives on as a program that, or so the story goes, hunts for the unwary." -The Professor

cards.name: Himitsu-Bako
cards.text:
1[credit]: Add Himitsu-Bako to HQ.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: Himitsu-Bako is a simple ice barrier that appears as a digital puzzle box. What makes it special is the ease with which it can be uninstalled and installed in a different server, throwing up barriers in unexpected places and giving any intruder a curious feeling of déjà vu.

cards.name: Hostage
cards.text: As an additional cost to play this event, spend [click]. Search your stack for a connection, reveal it, and add it to your grip. You may install that connection (paying its install cost). Shuffle your stack.

cards.name: Invasion of Privacy
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this operation, spend [click].
Trace[2]. If successful, reveal the grip. Trash up to X resources and/or events revealed this way, where X is equal to the amount by which your trace strength exceeded the Runner's link strength. If unsuccessful, take 1 bad publicity.

cards.name: Jackson Howard
cards.text: [click]: Draw 2 cards. Remove Jackson Howard from the game: Shuffle up to 3 cards from Archives into R&D.
cards.flavor: "It is my job to ensure our creations are the perfect companions and edutainment for tomorrow's consumers."

cards.name: John Masanori
cards.text:
The first time you make a successful run each turn, draw 1 card.
The first time you make an unsuccessful run each turn, take 1 tag.
cards.flavor: "I've been logging online with babes all day. Don't worry, the connections are clean. I guarantee it."

cards.name: Lockpick
cards.text: 1[recurring-credit] Use this credit to pay for using decoders.
cards.flavor: "I originally designed it for someone else, but it was so useful I decided to keep it for myself." -Kate "Mac" McCaffrey

cards.name: Motivation
cards.text: When your turn begins, you may look at the top card of your stack.
cards.flavor: Normal people-sane people-do not embark on a life of cybercrime. Who can say what motivates the deranged mind? An imagined slight, personal failings blamed on external forces, or the ever-popular lust for money? -Michael Muhama, Musings on Cybercrime

cards.name: NEXT Bronze
cards.text: NEXT Bronze has +1 strength for each rezzed piece of NEXT ice. [subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: NEXT Design's ice provides the discerning business with a suite of ice that creates a daunting security presence for intruders.

cards.name: Pawn
cards.text: [click]: Host this program on the outermost piece of ice protecting a central server. Whenever you make a successful run while this program is hosted on a piece of ice, host it on the next inward piece of ice. If you cannot, trash this program and install 1 other Caïssa program from your grip or heap, ignoring all costs.

cards.name: Project Ares
cards.text: When you score this agenda, the Runner trashes 1 of their installed cards for each hosted advancement counter past 4. If the Runner trashes at least 1 card this way, take 1 bad publicity.
cards.flavor: Who wants to start a war?

cards.name: Rook
cards.text: While this program is hosted on ice, the rez cost of each piece of ice protecting this server is increased by 2. [click]: Host this program on a piece of ice that is not hosting a Caïssa program. If this program is hosted on ice, its [click] ability can only be used to host it on ice protecting the same server or in the same position as its current host ice. (Count positions from the innermost ice.)

cards.name: Swarm
cards.text:
When you rez this ice, take 1 bad publicity.
You can advance this ice. It gains "[subroutine] Trash 1 installed program unless the Runner pays 3[credit]." for each hosted advancement counter.

cards.name: Bishop
cards.text: Host ice gets -2 strength. [click]: Host this program on a piece of ice that is not hosting a Caïssa program. If this program is hosted on ice protecting a central server, its [click] ability can only be used to host it on ice protecting a remote server. If this program is hosted on ice protecting a remote server, its [click] ability can only be used to host it on ice protecting a central server.

cards.name: Clone Retirement
cards.text:
When you score this agenda, you may remove 1 bad publicity.
When the Runner steals this agenda, take 1 bad publicity.
cards.flavor: "They call it 'retirement'. I call it 'euthanasia'." -Ken "Express" Tenma

cards.name: Copycat
cards.text: Whenever you pass a piece of ice, you may trash Copycat. If you do, choose another rezzed copy of that piece of ice protecting any server. The run continues as if you had just passed the chosen piece of ice (you are now running from the new position).
cards.flavor: The copycat function should be used with extreme caution, or you might end up on the wrong side of cyberspace.

cards.name: Elizabeth Mills
cards.text: When you rez this asset, remove 1 bad publicity. [click], [trash]: Trash 1 installed location resource. Take 1 bad publicity.
cards.flavor: "It's not personal. Urban renewal is a necessity of the modern world. It's always someone's home, yours is no different."

cards.name: Eureka!
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this event, spend [click].
Reveal the top card of your stack. You may install that card, lowering the install cost by 10[credit], if able; otherwise, trash it.
cards.flavor: "I've got a surprise for you."

cards.name: Hard at Work
cards.text: When your turn begins, gain 2[credit] and lose [click].
cards.flavor: Noise decided to go back to school. He applied for research grants at fifteen of the most prestigious universities. Then he hacked in and approved his applications. Breakfast time.

cards.name: Hellion Alpha Test
cards.text:
Play only if the Runner installed a resource during their last turn.
Trace[2]. If successful, add 1 installed resource to the top of the stack. If unsuccessful, take 1 bad publicity.

cards.name: Leviathan
cards.text: Interface → 3[credit]: Break up to 3 code gate subroutines. 3[credit]: +5 strength.
cards.flavor: It's efficient as all hell, for certain very large values of "efficient". The whale avatar is either a nice touch or a tragic misapplication of programmer man-hour, depending on who you ask. -BT's Guide to Icebreaking

cards.name: Muckraker
cards.text:
When you rez this ice, take 1 bad publicity.
[subroutine] Trace[1]. If successful, give the Runner 1 tag.
[subroutine] Trace[2]. If successful, give the Runner 1 tag.
[subroutine] Trace[3]. If successful, give the Runner 1 tag.
[subroutine] End the run if the Runner is tagged.

cards.name: Off the Grid
cards.text:
Install only in a remote server.
The Runner cannot initiate a run on this server.
Whenever the Runner makes a successful run on HQ, trash Off the Grid.

cards.name: Prepaid VoicePAD
cards.text: 1[recurring-credit] (When you install this card and before your turn begins, refill to 1 hosted credit.) You can spend hosted credits to play events.
cards.flavor: A VoicePAD is a personal access device with most of its functions ripped out. Just about all it's good for is making voice-calls and managing your contacts. The only reason to even have one is for its anonymity, which for a certain kind of person is all the reason one needs.

cards.name: Profiteering
cards.text: When you score this agenda, take up to 3 bad publicity. Gain 5[credit] for each bad publicity taken this way.
cards.flavor: It was surprisingly easy to make creds…if you didn't care about how you made them.

cards.name: Recon
cards.text: Make a run. You may jack out when you encounter the first piece of ice.
cards.flavor: Just like in the real world, sometimes it is best to send in the clone to do the dirty work.

cards.name: Record Reconstructor
cards.text: Whenever you make a successful run on Archives, instead of breaching Archives, you may add 1 faceup card from Archives to the top of R&D.
