cards.flavor: "Why is data deleted? Maybe they don't want it to be found. Or maybe it's just useless. The useless data is the kind you want." -The Professor

cards.name: Restructure
cards.text: Gain 15[credit].
cards.flavor: There are many names for those in the Administration Department. But if you like your job, you just refer to them as "sir" and "ma'am".

cards.name: Scheherazade
cards.text:
Scheherazade can host any number of programs.
Whenever you install a program on Scheherazade, gain 1[credit].
cards.flavor: Installing 1001 programs puts you in the hacker hall of fame, or would if such an institution actually existed.

cards.name: Shipment from SanSan
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this operation, spend [click].
Place up to 2 advancement tokens on a card that can be advanced.
cards.flavor: He signed for it, hand shaking in anticipation.

cards.name: Swordsman
cards.text: The Runner cannot break subroutines on this ice using AI programs. [subroutine] Trash 1 installed AI program. [subroutine] Do 1 net damage.
cards.flavor: Writing a program that can pass the Turing test is easy. The Gibson-Akamatsu test is a higher bar, and the only AIs to clear it thus far have been the androids. Even some humans have been known to fail.

cards.name: The Cleaners
cards.text: [interrupt] → Whenever you would do meat damage, increase that damage by 1.
cards.flavor: "I use bioroids because I can wipe their memories or just blow their brains out when the job is done. No witnesses means no witnesses."

cards.name: Wotan
cards.text:
[subroutine] End the run unless the Runner spends [click][click].
[subroutine] End the run unless the Runner pays 3[credit].
[subroutine] End the run unless the Runner trashes 1 installed program.
[subroutine] End the run unless the Runner suffers 1 core damage.

cards.name: Accelerated Diagnostics
cards.text: Look at the top 3 cards of R&D. If any of those cards are operations, you may play them (paying their play cost), ignoring any additional costs. Trash the rest of the unplayed cards you looked at.
cards.flavor: "I'm getting a reading that is…off the charts. No, it crashed the charts. That counts as off, right?"

cards.name: City Surveillance
cards.text: When the Runner's turn begins, give them 1 tag unless they pay 1[credit].
cards.flavor: Who watches the watcher? Probably another camera.

cards.name: Deep Red
cards.text: +3[mu] Use the MU on Deep Red only for Caïssa programs. Whenever you install a Caïssa program, you may trigger its [click] ability without spending [click]. Limit 1 console per player.

cards.name: Expert Schedule Analyzer
cards.text: [click]: Run HQ. If successful, instead of breaching HQ, you may reveal all cards in HQ.
cards.flavor: Knowing is half the battle. The easy half, anyway.

cards.name: Grifter
cards.text: When your turn ends, gain 1[credit] if you made a successful run this turn; otherwise, trash Grifter.
cards.flavor: With modern secretaries, incoming data can be filtered, sorted, tagged, and even sold without the intervention of a human user. In fact, given the zettabytes of data that might flood into a rig on a successful run, a human user could be considered useless ornamentation.

cards.name: Hudson 1.0
cards.text: Lose [click]: Break 1 subroutine on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. [subroutine] The Runner cannot access more than 1 card during this run. [subroutine] The Runner cannot access more than 1 card during this run.
cards.flavor: I'm not here to play games. The game is over.

cards.name: Interns
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this operation, spend [click].
Install a non-operation card from Archives or HQ, ignoring the install cost.
cards.flavor: "They're the only labor cheaper than clones."

cards.name: Ireress
cards.text: This ice gains "[subroutine] The Runner loses 1[credit]." for each bad publicity you have.
cards.flavor: Say it really fast.

cards.name: Isabel McGuire
cards.text: [click]: Add 1 of your installed cards to HQ.
cards.flavor: Even with a virtual ball, it is considered rude not to yell "Fore!"

cards.name: Knight
cards.text: Interface → 2[credit]: Break 1 subroutine on host ice. [click]: Host this program on a piece of ice that is not hosting a Caïssa program. If this program is hosted on ice, its [click] ability cannot be used to host it on the next inward or outward piece of ice.
cards.flavor: 'Maneuver warfare' is a doctrine that advocates keeping an enemy off-balance. It works just as well in cyberspace as in reality.

cards.name: Paper Wall
cards.text:
When the Runner fully breaks this ice, trash it.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: It folds under pressure.

cards.name: Power Shutdown
cards.text:
Play only if the Runner made a run during their last turn.
Trash any number of cards from the top of R&D. The Runner trashes an installed program or piece of hardware with an install cost equal to or less than the number of cards you trashed this way.

cards.name: Raymond Flint
cards.text: Whenever the Corp takes bad publicity, breach HQ. You cannot access cards in the root of HQ during this breach. [trash]: Expose 1 card.
cards.flavor:
"Flint? He's a burnout. A useless, alcoholic waste of Department time and money." -Louis Blaine, NAPD Detective.
"One of the best detectives on my PI list." -Richard Harrison, NAPD Captain.

cards.name: Reina Roja: Freedom Fighter
cards.text: The first piece of ice the Corp rezzes each turn costs 1[credit] more to rez.
cards.flavor: "Analyzing the board won't help. Your mistake was thinking we're playing the same game."

cards.name: Running Interference
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this event, spend [click].
Make a run. During this run, the Corp must pay X[credit] as an additional cost to rez each piece of ice, where X is the rez cost of that ice.

cards.name: Snoop
cards.text: When the Runner encounters Snoop, reveal all cards in the Runner's grip. Hosted power counter: Reveal all cards in the Runner's grip. Trash 1 of those cards. [subroutine] Trace[3]. If successful, place 1 power counter on Snoop.

cards.name: Sundew
cards.text: The first time the Runner spends 1 or more [click] during their turn, gain 2[credit]. If those [click] were spent to take an action, the first time during that action a run on this server begins, pay 2[credit].
cards.flavor: As beautiful as it is dangerous. And it's plenty dangerous.

cards.name: Torch
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 code gate subroutine. 1[credit]: +1 strength.
cards.flavor: The core of the grid. A blinding sphere of light, teeming with energy, crackling with flame. Beyond were only twinkling bits of data in a field of darkness. No hacker dared approach the core, except one. He came back with a flare of code, a torch that burned with the fire of the core itself. The dark places of cyberspace were dark no more, and the legend of g00ru was born.

cards.name: Unorthodox Predictions
cards.text: When you score Unorthodox Predictions, choose sentry, code gate or barrier. Subroutines on ice of the chosen type cannot be broken until the beginning of your next turn.

cards.name: Woman in the Red Dress
cards.text: When your turn begins, reveal the top card of R&D. The Corp may draw that card.
cards.flavor: Looks can be deceiving.

cards.name: Activist Support
cards.text:
When the Corp's turn begins, take 1 tag if you have no tags.
When your turn begins, give the Corp 1 bad publicity if they have no bad publicity.
cards.flavor: "They call me a terrorist to scare people. If they want to find terrorists, maybe they should start by looking in the mirror." -Reina Roja

cards.name: Capstone
cards.text: [click]: Trash any number of cards from your grip. For each trashed card of which you have another copy installed, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: "Once you have achieved perfection, what's next?" -The Professor

cards.name: Curtain Wall
cards.text:
If Curtain Wall is the outermost piece of ice protecting a server, it has +4 strength.
[subroutine] End the run.
[subroutine] End the run.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor:
[subroutine] End the game.
Just kidding.

cards.name: Fenris
cards.text:
When you rez this ice, take 1 bad publicity.
[subroutine] Do 1 core damage.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: As reported cases of brain damage in veterans rise, mind/machine interface devices are subject to increased public scrutiny. That certain programs can cause irreparable harm to users has gone from fringe theory to accepted truth.

cards.name: Garrote
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 sentry subroutine. 1[credit]: +1 strength.
cards.flavor: The first credited icebreaker was nothing more than a unique script to bypass the security calls on a Gibson 3 Data Sentry. Garrote has over 20,000 times the data as that first breaker, but the idea remains the same: cut off the power source from the network, and then smash on through.

cards.name: Keyhole
cards.text: [click]: Run R&D. If successful, instead of breaching R&D, look at the top 3 cards of R&D. Trash 1 of those cards, then the Corp shuffles R&D.
cards.flavor: The instructions claim that it sifts the most important data. 'Important', it has been found, is a highly relative term.

cards.name: LLDS Processor
cards.text: Whenever you install an icebreaker, that icebreaker has +1 strength until the end of the turn.
cards.flavor: LLDS Unlimited was born the day two designers answered the question "Why doesn't anyone make Diesel for computers?"

cards.name: Lawyer Up
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this event, spend [click].
Remove up to 2 tags and draw 3 cards.
cards.flavor: Pros don't need to call their lawyer. Pros have their secretary rigged to do it for them if they ever go off-grid.

cards.name: Leverage
cards.text:
Play only if you made a successful run on HQ this turn.
The Corp may take 2 bad publicity. If they do not, whenever you would take damage until your next turn begins, prevent all of that damage.
cards.flavor: "Care to have a look?"

cards.name: Panic Button
cards.text:
Install only in the root of HQ.
1[credit]: Draw 1 card. Use this ability only during a run on HQ.
cards.flavor: The button didn't seem to do anything. So he pushed it again. And again. And again.

cards.name: Punitive Counterstrike
cards.text: Trace[5]. If successful, do X meat damage. X is equal to the sum of the printed agenda points on all agendas the Runner stole during their last turn.
cards.flavor: "I'd say it's nothing personal, but corporations are people, too."

cards.name: RSVP
cards.text: [subroutine] The Runner cannot spend any credits for the remainder of this run.
cards.flavor: This ice disguises itself as a series of electronic transactions, tying up the runner's funds in a thousand or so non-existent purchases and refunds. The banks' system of holds and checks means that while not a single credit ever leaves their servers the runner has no available funds. RSVP also has the unfortunate side effect of being entirely legal…strictly speaking.

cards.name: Rex Campaign
cards.text:
When you rez this asset, load 3 power counters onto it. When it is empty, trash it and either remove 1 bad publicity or gain 5[credit].
When your turn begins, remove 1 hosted power counter.

cards.name: Sharpshooter
cards.text: Interface → [trash]: Break any number of destroyer subroutines. 1[credit]: +2 strength.
cards.flavor: "One-shot icebreakers are popular among many of my protégés. They don't have the patience for the hunt." -The Professor

cards.name: Shock!
cards.text:
While the Runner is accessing this asset in R&D, they must reveal it.
When the Runner accesses this asset, do 1 net damage.

cards.name: Starlight Crusade Funding
cards.text: When your turn begins, lose [click]. Ignore any additional costs on each double event you play.
cards.flavor: "I like to say 'Traditional values for a modern time.' War in space and life made by human hands, machines smart enough to ask if they have souls…Religion is as important and relevent now as at any time in human history. We must rise to meet the new challenges. And we must have faith."

cards.name: Sweeps Week
cards.text: Gain 1[credit] for each card in the Runner's grip.
cards.flavor:
"Let me get this straight. Your target market is 15-19 year old g-modded immigrants with one parent, a discretionary income over 2k a month, B+ or higher grades, an outgoing personality, and have a friend who owns a g-monkey?"
"Yes. Is that a problem?"
"No, not at all. I just don't get why your list is so short."

cards.name: TGTBT
cards.text:
While the Runner is accessing this agenda in R&D, they must reveal it.
When the Runner accesses this agenda, give them 1 tag.
cards.flavor: "The damn raven just kind of cawed at me as I went past. I should have known it was too good to be true."

cards.name: Tsurugi
cards.text:
[subroutine] End the run unless the Corp pays 1[credit].
[subroutine] Do 1 net damage.
[subroutine] Do 1 net damage.
[subroutine] Do 1 net damage.
cards.flavor: "It's ice so dangerous it has safety protocols. Think about that." -g00ru

cards.name: Veterans Program
cards.text: When you score this agenda, you may remove up to 2 bad publicity.
cards.flavor: It's easy to replace limbs. It's more difficult to replace memories.

cards.name: Alpha
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 subroutine. 1[credit]: +1 strength. This program can only interface with the outermost piece of ice protecting a server.
cards.flavor: The beginning…

cards.name: Blackguard
cards.text: +2[mu] Whenever you expose a card, the Corp must rez it by paying its rez cost, if able. Limit 1 console per player.
cards.flavor: The power of the focused mind is a power beyond comprehension.

cards.name: Blackmail
cards.text:
Play only if the Corp has at least 1 bad publicity.
Run any server. The Corp cannot rez ice during that run.

cards.name: Blue Level Clearance
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this operation, spend [click].
Gain 5[credit] and draw 2 cards.
cards.flavor: Blue-one level clearance doesn't exist. And if it did exist, you wouldn't be cleared to know about it.

cards.name: CyberSolutions Mem Chip
cards.flavor: "CyberSolutions is a boring name for a company that makes pretty exciting products. Their memory chips have some pretty tricky stuff going on inside and I keep hearing good things about their M/MI implants. I even heard they were on the path to their own androids about a year ago. I wonder whatever happened with that?" -Kate "Mac" McCaffrey

cards.name: Executive Wiretaps
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this event, spend [click].
Reveal all cards in HQ.
cards.flavor: "When you need someone who is a little more hands on, look me up." -Silhouette

cards.name: GRNDL Refinery
cards.text:
GRNDL Refinery can be advanced.
[click], [trash]: Gain 4[credit] for each advancement token on GRNDL Refinery.
cards.flavor: GRNDL refineries process many different rare elements unearthed during the fracking process.

cards.name: GRNDL: Power Unleashed
cards.text: You start the game with 10[credit] and 1 bad publicity.
cards.flavor: Geostrategic Research and Neothermal Development Laboratories

cards.name: Hemorrhage
cards.text: Whenever you make a successful run, place 1 virus counter on Hemorrhage. [click], 2 hosted virus counters: The Corp trashes 1 card from HQ.
cards.flavor: Bleeding data is more of a science than an art. Too much and you can end up with a one-way ticket to flatline city. Not enough and you might as well be running an empty server.

cards.name: Market Research
cards.text:
If the Runner is tagged when you score Market Research, place 1 agenda counter on it.
Market Research is worth 1 additional agenda point while it has an agenda counter on it.

cards.name: Omega
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 subroutine. 1[credit]: +1 strength. This program can only interface with the innermost piece of ice protecting a server.
cards.flavor: …and the end?

cards.name: Quest Completed
cards.text:
Play only if you made a successful run on R&D, HQ, and Archives this turn.
Access 1 installed card (non-ice).
cards.flavor:
That moment of bliss. That feeling of accomplishment. That certainty of purpose.
What's next?

cards.name: Restoring Face
cards.text: Reveal and trash 1 of your installed sysop, executive, or clone cards. If you do, remove up to 2 bad publicity.
cards.flavor: He slowly pried open the lid, and the tantō glinted madly in the half-light. The executive motioned to the blade. Looks like the meeting was being cut short.

cards.name: Strongbox
cards.text: Persistent → As an additional cost to steal an agenda from this server or its root, the Runner must spend [click]. (If the Runner trashes this card while accessing it, this ability still applies for the remainder of this run.)

cards.name: Subliminal Messaging
cards.text:
Gain 1[credit].
The first time each turn you play a copy of Subliminal Messaging, gain [click].
When your turn begins, if this card is in Archives and the Runner did not initiate any runs during their last turn, you may reveal this card and add it to HQ.

cards.name: Tallie Perrault
cards.text: Whenever a gray ops or black ops operation is trashed after resolving, you may give the Corp 1 bad publicity and take 1 tag. [trash]: Draw 1 card for each bad publicity the Corp has.
cards.flavor: Stick with your plan and you'll be fine. Stick with the plan.

cards.name: Toshiyuki Sakai
cards.text:
Toshiyuki Sakai can be advanced.
If Toshiyuki Sakai is accessed while installed, you may swap him with an agenda or asset from HQ. The new agenda or asset is installed unrezzed, and keeps all advancement tokens on Toshiyuki Sakai. The Runner can choose not to access the new card.

cards.name: Vulcan Coverup
cards.text:
When you score this agenda, do 2 meat damage.
When the Runner steals this agenda, take 1 bad publicity.
cards.flavor: "I did warn you that leaks would have to be patched."

cards.name: Wraparound
cards.text: While there are no installed fracter programs, this ice gets +7 strength. [subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: "It can make a real fine roller coaster, provided you're properly stimmed up." -Noise

cards.name: Yagura
cards.text:
[subroutine] Look at the top card of R&D. You may add that card to the bottom of R&D.
[subroutine] Do 1 net damage.
cards.flavor: The 'cyber-war' is a war of information, and in a war of information, advance warning can be as good as a killing blow. -Michael Muhama, Musings on Cybercrime

cards.name: Broadcast Square
cards.text: [interrupt] → Whenever you would take bad publicity, trace[3]. If successful, prevent all of that bad publicity.
cards.flavor: Tourists have flocked to Broadcast Square in even greater numbers ever since the notorious Ho-meh's crime spree ended there in a hail of flechettes. Well, that's how it happened in the sensie.

cards.name: Caprice Nisei
cards.text: Whenever the Runner passes all of the ice protecting this server, you and the Runner secretly spend 0[credit], 1[credit], or 2[credit]. Reveal spent credits. If you and the Runner spent a different number of credits, end the run.
cards.flavor: The first clone to serve as an NAPD detective.

cards.name: Corporate Shuffle
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this operation, spend [click].
Shuffle all cards in HQ into R&D. Draw 5 cards.
cards.flavor: The only thing worse than being fired and replaced by a younger, cheaper worker? Being replaced by an android.

cards.name: Dyson Fractal Generator
cards.text: 1[recurring-credit] Use this credit to pay for using fracters.
cards.flavor: The Dyson Fractal Generator is a useless lump of silicon; all it does is produce truly random results. What kind of madman slaps that in his rig? What's the use of a totally random number? -John Masanori

cards.name: Fall Guy
cards.text: [interrupt] → [trash]: Prevent a player from trashing another installed resource. [trash]: Gain 2[credit].
cards.flavor: There are good, honest, hardworking cops in the NAPD. Officers who do their best to bring justice to the guilty and protect the innocent. Fortunately for the criminals, they're outnumbered by the other kind. The kind who are much easier to work with.

cards.name: Gyri Labyrinth
cards.text: [subroutine] The Runner's maximum hand size is reduced by 2 until the beginning of the Corp's next turn.
cards.flavor: Once inside, the only way out is through your own mind.

cards.name: Hive
cards.text:
This ice loses 1 of its printed "[subroutine] End the run." subroutines for each agenda point in your score area.
[subroutine] End the run.
[subroutine] End the run.
[subroutine] End the run.
[subroutine] End the run.
[subroutine] End the run.

cards.name: Lucky Find
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this event, spend [click].
Gain 9[credit].
cards.flavor: Data hunters always pay top dollar for old drives. The more useless the data, the higher the payout.

cards.name: Marker
cards.text: [subroutine] The next piece of ice the Runner encounters during this run gains "[subroutine] End the run." after its other subroutines for the remainder of that run.
cards.flavor: "It doesn't do anything in and of itself. It just marks you as an intruder and makes the next ice do all the work." -Kate "Mac" McCaffrey

cards.name: NAPD Contract
cards.text:
This agenda gets +1 advancement requirement for each bad publicity you have.
As an additional cost to steal this agenda, the Runner must pay 4[credit].

cards.name: Paintbrush
cards.text: [click]: Choose a rezzed piece of ice. That ice gains sentry, code gate or barrier until the end of the next run this turn.
cards.flavor: "Hand-made code is like hand-made art. You can see the brush strokes, which lets you see the artist. And then you can see everything in a new way." -Kate "Mac" McCaffrey

cards.name: Power Nap
cards.text: As an additional cost to play this event, spend [click]. Gain 2[credit]. Gain an additional 1[credit] for each double event in your heap.
cards.flavor: "When I said I could hack it in my sleep, did you think I was joking?" -Chaos Theory

cards.name: Quandary
cards.text: [subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: It wants to have two subroutines when it grows up.

cards.name: Queen's Gambit
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this event, spend [click].
Place up to 3 advancement counters on 1 unrezzed card in the root of a remote server. Gain 2[credit] for each counter placed this way. You cannot access that card for the remainder of the turn.

cards.name: Reclamation Order
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this operation, spend [click].
Name a card other than Reclamation Order. Reveal any number of copies of the named card from Archives and add them to HQ.

cards.name: Savoir-faire
cards.text:
You cannot use Savoir-faire more than once each turn.
2[credit]: Install a program from your grip, paying the install cost.
cards.flavor: "Predictive algorithms that fetch you the program you need before you even know you need it. My second favorite lady." -Gabriel Santiago

cards.name: Shinobi
cards.text:
When you rez this ice, take 1 bad publicity.
[subroutine] Trace[1]. If successful, do 1 net damage.
[subroutine] Trace[2]. If successful, do 2 net damage.
[subroutine] Trace[3]. If successful, do 3 net damage and end the run.

cards.name: Silencer
cards.text: 1[recurring-credit] Use this credit to pay for using killers.
cards.flavor: Take Moore's Law, iterate it over a century or two, and mix in quantum computing. You get to the point where you're developing the software on a hardware platform that you design at the same time. Tailor-made for each other. Exciting time to be alive! -William Knuth, The Tower of Babbage

cards.name: Singularity
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this event, spend [click].
Run a remote server. If successful, instead of breaching that server, trash all cards installed in the root of that server.

cards.name: Witness Tampering
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this operation, spend [click].
Remove up to 2 bad publicity.
cards.flavor: "Now, let's talk about how little you remember of the events of June sixth through sixteenth."

cards.name: Alias
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 sentry subroutine. 2[credit]: +3 strength. This program cannot interface with ice protecting a remote server.
cards.flavor: Appearances are easy to change in cyberspace, but a high-quality render is not easy to mimic.

cards.name: Breach
cards.text: Interface → 2[credit]: Break up to 3 barrier subroutines. 2[credit]: +4 strength. This program cannot interface with ice protecting a remote server.

cards.name: Bug
cards.text:
Install only if you made a successful run on HQ this turn.
Whenever the Corp draws a card, you may pay 2[credit] to reveal that card.
cards.flavor: The digital equivalent of a fly on the wall.

cards.name: Calling in Favors
cards.text: Gain 1[credit] for each installed connection resource.
cards.flavor: A job is only as strong as the weakest link. Thankfully Ms. Jones is always on time.

cards.name: Cerebral Cast
cards.text:
Play only if the Runner made a successful run during their last turn.
You and the Runner secretly spend 0[credit], 1[credit], or 2[credit]. Reveal spent credits. If you and the Runner spent a different number of credits, they must suffer 1 core damage or take 1 tag.

cards.name: Chairman Hiro
cards.text:
The Runner gets -2 maximum hand size.
When this asset is trashed from anywhere while being accessed, add it to the Runner's score area as an agenda worth 2 agenda points.

cards.name: Diversified Portfolio
cards.text: Gain 1[credit] for each remote server with a card in its root.
cards.flavor: YucaBean has seen astounding growth in even the most remote markets.

cards.name: Donut Taganes
cards.text: The play cost of operations and events is increased by 1.
cards.flavor: You can find Donut in the park on Thursday afternoons, playing backgammon. You want his attention, the price is always the same: a cup of coffee and a donut. That buys you a seat at the backgammon table, and you have until he beats you to talk business and set the price.

cards.name: Early Bird
cards.text:
Play only as your first click.
Gain [click]. Run any server.
cards.flavor: Tenma clones are excellent at multitasking, their brains custom-made for parallel processing.

cards.name: Express Delivery
cards.text: Look at the top 4 cards of your stack and add 1 of those cards to your grip. Shuffle your stack.
cards.flavor: The clone was surprised to see the red-jacketed man. It was like looking in a mirror, only the mirror made him look…cool. Confident. Individual.

cards.name: Fast Track
cards.text: Search R&D for an agenda, reveal it, and add it to HQ. Shuffle R&D.
cards.flavor: The longer the employees didn't look at the Doomsday Clock, the more it gnawed at the back of their minds. A quick look only reinforced what they already knew: there wasn't enough time.

cards.name: Feint
cards.text: Run HQ. The first 2 times this run you encounter a piece of ice, bypass that ice. If successful, you cannot breach HQ.
cards.flavor: Stirling entered the server, passing a growling piece of ice. He was unarmed…or so it seemed.

cards.name: Gingerbread
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 tracer subroutine. 2[credit]: +3 strength.
cards.flavor: Catch me if you can!

cards.name: Grappling Hook
cards.text: [trash]: Break all but 1 subroutine on a piece of ice.
cards.flavor: If speed is of the essence, an indirect encounter with a piece of ice is usually best.

cards.name: Guard
cards.text:
Guard cannot be bypassed.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: Out of the corner of his vision, a flash of light. He felt a thud as his grip on cyberspace loosened. Spider didn't like this. He should have bypassed the outer layer of ice by jacking in from the internal server. Another thud, and his whole frame shook with the resounding shockwave. He desperately reached for his shuriken…

cards.name: Harmony Medtech: Biomedical Pioneer
cards.text: Each player needs 1 fewer agenda point to win the game.
cards.flavor: Evolving a Better You.

cards.name: House of Knives
cards.text: When you score this agenda, place 3 agenda counters on it. Hosted agenda counter: Do 1 net damage. Use this ability only during a run and only once per run.

cards.name: Iain Stirling: Retired Spook
cards.text: When your turn begins, gain 2[credit] if the Corp has more scored agenda points than you.
cards.flavor: "Truth is a fickle mistress."

cards.name: Inazuma
cards.text:
[subroutine] During the next encounter this run, the Runner cannot break subroutines on the encountered ice.
[subroutine] The Runner cannot jack out this run until after their next encounter with a piece of ice begins.
cards.flavor: Trapped in their own reality, a paralyzed runner cannot even jack out.

cards.name: Ken “Express” Tenma: Disappeared Clone
cards.text: The first time each turn you play a run event, gain 1[credit].
cards.flavor: "Try to keep up."

cards.name: Komainu
cards.text: When the Runner encounters this ice, it gains X "[subroutine] Do 1 net damage." subroutines for the remainder of this run. X is equal to the number of cards in the grip.

cards.name: Legwork
cards.text: Run HQ. If successful, access 2 additional cards when you breach HQ.
cards.flavor: "I work by referral only, with an up-front fee. The fee is reasonable if you value results." -Silhouette

cards.name: Logos
cards.text: +1[mu] Your maximum hand size is increased by 1. Whenever the Corp scores an agenda, you may search your stack for a card and add it to your grip. Shuffle your stack. Limit 1 console per player.

cards.name: Mass Install
cards.text: Install up to 3 programs from your grip (paying the install costs).
cards.flavor: "Welcome to the mass install wizard! This wizard will guide you through the process of installing a whole mess of programs onto your almost-certainly inadequate rig. When you're ready to continue, say-oops, too late, here we go!"

cards.name: Medical Breakthrough
cards.text: Lower the advancement requirement of each Medical Breakthrough by 1. This ability is active even while Medical Breakthrough is in the Runner's score area.
cards.flavor: "You won't feel it. Or anything else, for that matter."

cards.name: Medical Research Fundraiser
cards.text: Gain 8[credit]. The Runner gains 3[credit].
cards.flavor: "Together we have all but eradicated natural diseases from the face of this planet. The new spectre of synthetic disease-of bioterrorism-demands that we continue our efforts."

cards.name: Mental Health Clinic
cards.text:
Gain 1[credit] when your turn begins.
The Runner's maximum hand size is increased by 1.
cards.flavor: The whitewashed walls dropped away and a beautiful zen garden appeared. It was all an illusion, but it was a comforting illusion.

cards.name: Mushin No Shin
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this operation, spend [click].
Install 1 asset, agenda, or upgrade from HQ in the root of a new server. Place 3 advancement counters on that card. You cannot score or rez that card until your next turn begins.

cards.name: NeoTokyo Grid
cards.text: The first time each turn an advancement counter is placed on a card in the root of this server, gain 1[credit]. Limit 1 region per server.
cards.flavor: It is difficult to go to Japan without ending up in the sprawl of NeoTokyo.

cards.name: Nisei Division: The Next Generation
cards.text: Whenever you and the Runner reveal secretly spent credits, gain 1[credit].
cards.flavor: Perfecting the Imperfect.

cards.name: Oracle May
cards.text: You cannot use this resource more than once per turn. [click]: Choose a card type. Reveal the top card of your stack. If that card has the chosen type, draw it and gain 2[credit]. Otherwise, trash it.
cards.flavor: "The best place to hide is in plain sight, don't you think?"

cards.name: Overmind
cards.text: When you install this program, place 1 power counter on it for each unused MU. (Place counters after this program's MU cost applies.) Interface → Hosted power counter: Break 1 subroutine. 1[credit]: +1 strength.

cards.name: Passport
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 code gate subroutine. 2[credit]: +2 strength. This program cannot interface with ice protecting a remote server.
cards.flavor: Nothing is secure when you have the right documentation.

cards.name: Philotic Entanglement
cards.text:
When you score Philotic Entanglement, do 1 net damage for each agenda in the Runner's score area.
Limit 1 Philotic Entanglement per deck.

cards.name: Plan B
cards.text:
Plan B can be advanced.
If the Runner accesses Plan B, you may reveal and score an agenda from HQ with an advancement requirement equal to or less than the number of advancement tokens on Plan B.

cards.name: Planned Assault
cards.text: As an additional cost to play this event, spend [click]. Search your stack for a run event and play that run event (paying its play cost), ignoring any additional costs. Shuffle your stack.

cards.name: Psychic Field
cards.text: If the Runner exposes or accesses Psychic Field while installed, you and the Runner secretly spend 0[credit], 1[credit], or 2[credit]. Reveal spent credits. If you and the Runner spent a different number of credits, do 1 net damage for each card in the Runner's grip.

cards.name: Public Terminal
cards.text: 1[recurring-credit] Use this credit to play run events.
cards.flavor: Express loved libraries. The consoles were weak, but the security even weaker. He wirelessly loaded up his personal blend of code and started cloning the drive. In just a few minutes, another zombie would claw its way to the surface of cyberspace.

cards.name: Pup
cards.text:
[subroutine] Do 1 net damage unless the Runner pays 1[credit].
[subroutine] Do 1 net damage unless the Runner pays 1[credit].
cards.flavor: Yip Yip!

cards.name: Push Your Luck
cards.text: Secretly spend any number of credits. The Corp guesses if you spent an even or odd amount. Reveal spent credits. If the Corp guessed incorrectly, gain credits equal to twice the amount spent.

cards.name: Q-Coherence Chip
cards.text:
+1[mu]
When an installed program is trashed, trash this hardware.
cards.flavor: One of the core problems of quantum computing is isolating the system from external factors to prevent decoherence. The Q-Coherence Chip is one, imperfect, solution.

cards.name: Rainbow
cards.text: [subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: The annual review of ice as published by the NSCA consistently gives top marks to the ice that provide the most impact in relation to their size and upkeep cost. Critics of the NSCA point to the bounce ratio as the most important stat when judging ice.

cards.name: Security Testing
cards.text:
When your turn begins, you may choose a server.
The first time each turn you make a successful run on the chosen server, instead of breaching it, gain 2[credit].
cards.flavor: She was as good as Mr. Li said. The source machine had been compromised in under 24 hours. If a freelance operative could do that, the server clearly wasn't ready to endure Gagarin's legion of corp-owned runners.

cards.name: Shi.Kyū
cards.text: When the Runner accesses this asset anywhere except in R&D, spend any number of credits. The Runner suffers 1 net damage for each credit spent this way unless they add this asset to their score area as an agenda worth −1 agenda point.

cards.name: Shiro
cards.text:
[subroutine] Look at the top 3 cards of R&D and arrange them in any order.
[subroutine] You may pay 1[credit]. If you do not, the Runner breaches R&D. They cannot access cards in the root of R&D during that breach.
cards.flavor: When locked in a fortress in your own mind, be careful what door you open.

cards.name: Silhouette: Stealth Operative
cards.text: The first time you make a successful run on HQ each turn, you may expose 1 card.
cards.flavor: "Don't waste my time."

cards.name: Susanoo-no-Mikoto
cards.text: [subroutine] If the attacked server is not Archives, the Runner moves to the outermost position of Archives instead of passing this ice. The Runner cannot jack out this run until after they encounter a piece of ice.
cards.flavor: Certain areas of cyberspace are dominated by a single digital entity. Runners call them 'gods', and only a miracle can save those foolish enough to enter their domain.

cards.name: Tenma Line
cards.text: [click]: Swap 2 pieces of installed ice.
cards.flavor: The Tenma clones became Jinteki's third highest-grossing line ever due to the rapid urban expansion that occurred after the war. Their unparalleled reaction times, safety records, and punctuality have made them the top choice for shipping and transportation services.

cards.name: Tennin Institute: The Secrets Within
cards.text: When your turn begins, if the Runner did not make a successful run during their last turn, you may place 1 advancement counter on an installed card.

cards.name: The Future Perfect
cards.text: When the Runner accesses this agenda while it is not installed, play a Psi Game. (Players secretly bid 0–2[credit]. Then each player reveals and spends their bid.) If the bids differ, the Runner cannot steal this agenda during this access.

cards.name: Theophilius Bagbiter
cards.text:
When you install Theophilius Bagbiter, lose all credits in your credit pool.
Your maximum hand size is equal to the number of credits in your credit pool.
cards.flavor: "Why is a raven like a typing desk?"

cards.name: Tori Hanzō
cards.text: [interrupt] → The first time you would do 1 or more net damage during each run against this server, instead you may pay 2[credit] to do 1 core damage.
cards.flavor: Known as the Red Woman, Hanzō is notorious for her ruthless methods of server protection.

cards.name: Tri-maf Contact
cards.text: You cannot use this resource more than once per turn. [click]: Gain 2[credit]. When this resource is trashed, suffer 3 meat damage.
cards.flavor:
She slipped back onto her hopper. "I'm your family now, so don't twist me, dǒng ma?"
He flicked the e-cig away from his mouth, and nodded. What had he gotten himself into?

cards.name: Unregistered S&W '35
cards.text: Use this hardware only if you have made a successful run on HQ this turn. [click][click]: Trash 1 rezzed bioroid, clone, executive, or sysop in the root of a remote server.

cards.name: Window
cards.text: [click]: Draw 1 card from the bottom of your stack.
cards.flavor: The grass looked greener on the other side of the tear. But it always did, and there was always another tear.

cards.name: Bad Times
cards.text:
Play only if the Runner is tagged.
The Runner's memory limit is reduced by 2 until the end of the turn.
cards.flavor: Known as malware 0-394-41525-6 to sysops, runners just refer to it as "bad times."

cards.name: Cyber Threat
cards.text:
Play only as your first [click].
Choose a server. The Corp may rez 1 piece of ice protecting that server. If they do not, run that server. The Corp cannot rez ice during that run.

cards.name: Domestic Sleepers
cards.text:
[click],[click],[click]: Place 1 agenda counter on Domestic Sleepers.
Domestic Sleepers is worth 1 agenda point while it has at least 1 agenda counter on it.

cards.name: Eden Shard
cards.text: Whenever you make a successful run on R&D, instead of breaching R&D, you may install this resource from your grip, ignoring all costs. [trash]: The Corp draws 2 cards. Limit 1 per deck.

cards.name: Galahad
cards.text: When the Runner encounters this ice, you may reveal up to 2 pieces of grail ice in HQ. For the remainder of this run, this ice gains the subroutines of each revealed piece of ice in the order of your choice. [subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: He who bears the shield of honor.

cards.name: Lamprey
cards.text:
Whenever you make a successful run on HQ, the Corp loses 1[credit].
Trash Lamprey if the Corp purges virus counters.

cards.name: Leprechaun
cards.text: Leprechaun can host up to 2 programs. The memory costs of hosted programs do not count against your memory limit.
cards.flavor: "I once saw someone running a seven-tier nested daemon tree. Not for any good reason, just to see if he could. Well, of course the root daemon crashed and he lost everything. I wonder what he's up to now?" -Kate "Mac" McCaffrey

cards.name: Lotus Field
cards.text:
The strength of this ice cannot be lowered.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: "Chi resonance mapping has created a whole new field of network security. It is unassailable perfection." -Akitaro Watanabe

cards.name: Midway Station Grid
cards.text: During runs on this server, the Runner must pay 1[credit] as an additional cost to use an icebreaker ability to break subroutines. Limit 1 region per server.
cards.flavor: Halfway upstalk, Midway is a destination unto itself with its microgravity hotels and fine dining options.

cards.name: Mother Goddess
cards.text:
Mother Goddess gains the subtypes of all other rezzed ice.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: On the first day She breathed data into the void, and it hung suspended like jewelled stars. On the second day She spoke order into the data, and it flowed from rivulets into streams and from streams into mighty rivers. On the third day She gave independence to the order, and it ebbed and flowed according to its own accord. -The Cant of Helios

cards.name: Mutate
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this operation, trash a rezzed piece of ice.
Reveal cards from the top of R&D until you reveal a piece of ice. Install and rez that ice in the same position as the ice that was trashed, ignoring all costs. Shuffle R&D.

cards.name: NEXT Silver
cards.text: This ice gains "[subroutine] End the run." for each rezzed piece of NEXT ice.
cards.flavor: The networking capabilities of the NEXT suite of ice are unparalleled.

cards.name: Nasir Meidan: Cyber Explorer
cards.text: Whenever you encounter a piece of ice after an approach during which that ice was rezzed, lose all credits in your credit pool. Gain credits equal to the rez cost of that ice.

cards.name: Near-Earth Hub: Broadcast Center
cards.text: The first time each turn you create a remote server, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Only the News You Need.

cards.name: Paper Tripping
cards.text:
Play only as your first [click].
Remove all tags.
cards.flavor: His eyes were beginning to blur, as he duplicated the credentials for what seemed like the fiftieth time. Perhaps a genetic refit would have been easier.

cards.name: Power Tap
cards.text: Gain 1[credit] whenever a trace is initiated.
cards.flavor: "Public network kiosks, vending machines-there's all sorts of poorly-secured power sources in the city. Tap in to one of these and you've got plenty of juice when you need it. A little advance warning when the power grid starts misbehaving, too." -Gabriel Santiago

cards.name: Primary Transmission Dish
cards.text:
3[recurring-credit]
Use these credits during traces.
cards.flavor: Works better than a PAD hooked up to a tinfoil umbrella and coffee can.

cards.name: Social Engineering
cards.text:
Play only as your first [click].
Choose an unrezzed piece of ice. If the Corp rezzes that piece of ice this turn, gain credits equal to its rez cost.

cards.name: Taurus
cards.text: [subroutine] Trace[2]. If successful, trash 1 piece of hardware. If your trace strength is 5 or greater, trash 1 piece of hardware.
cards.flavor: Taurus promised strength, but gave only rage.

cards.name: The Root
cards.text:
3[recurring-credit]
Use these credits to advance, install, and rez cards.
cards.flavor: They said it couldn't be built. That it was a fantasy. That Jack Weyland was a fool, and he had bought the fools in Washington too. But year after year the buckyweave grew, and 'they' stopped talking.

cards.name: Cache
cards.text: Place 3 virus counters on Cache when it is installed. Hosted virus counter: Gain 1[credit].
cards.flavor: "People keep saying that 'Cash is king' in the business, like it's untraceable in the days of DNA sniffers and microtracers. Digital credits can be just as anonymous, and they're just as easy to counterfeit." -Silhouette

cards.name: Cerebral Static
cards.text: This operation is not trashed until another current is played or an agenda is stolen. The Runner's identity loses its printed abilities.
cards.flavor: Her eyes were the color of a vidscreen, tuned to a dead channel.

cards.name: D4v1d
cards.text: Place 3 power counters on D4v1d when it is installed. Hosted power counter: Break ice subroutine on a piece of ice that has a strength of 5 or greater.
cards.flavor: Sometimes a single stone is enough.

cards.name: Eden Fragment
cards.text:
Ignore the install cost of the first piece of ice you install each turn.
Limit 1 per deck.

cards.name: Encrypted Portals
cards.text: All code gate ice have +1 strength. When you score Encrypted Portals, gain 1[credit] for each rezzed code gate.
cards.flavor: "Binary computing is obsolete. I use a base-4 structure for this system; it's modeled on our DNA. Well, my DNA, anyway." -Doctor Endo, Jinteki researcher

cards.name: Enhanced Login Protocol
cards.text: This operation is not trashed until another current is played or an agenda is stolen. As an additional cost to take the basic action to run a server for the first time each turn, the Runner must spend [click].

cards.name: Ghost Runner
cards.text:
Place 3[credit] on Ghost Runner when it is installed. When there are no credits left on Ghost Runner, trash it.
You can use the credits on Ghost Runner during a run.
cards.flavor: In the spaces between the data, do trapped souls from the past persist?

cards.name: Heinlein Grid
cards.text: Whenever the Runner loses or spends [click] during a run on this server, they lose all credits in their credit pool. Limit 1 region per server.
cards.flavor: "There are many advantages to having facilities on the moon. Less traffic, for example." -Director Hass

cards.name: Information Overload
cards.text:
When the Runner encounters this ice, Trace[1]. If successful, give them 1 tag.
This ice gains "[subroutine] The Runner trashes 1 of their installed cards." for each tag the Runner has.
cards.flavor: Throw enough data at a runner and it ceases to have any meaning at all.

cards.name: LLDS Energy Regulator
cards.text: [interrupt] → 3[credit] or [trash]: Prevent a player from trashing 1 installed piece of hardware.
cards.flavor: Originally not very popular, the regulator was overlooked by those who used energy sinks to protect their rig. But it quickly found an audience once Smoke casted a run on a Blue Sun server, using it to keep her rig online while repeatedly diverting energy spikes in excess of 50,000 volts.

cards.name: Lag Time
cards.text: This operation is not trashed until another current is played or an agenda is stolen. All ice have +1 strength.
cards.flavor: "I don't care how good your console is, or how tricked out your rig is. The lag time on a run on the moon from earthside can be a killer." -Leela Patel

cards.name: Net Celebrity
cards.text: This card is not trashed until another current is played or an agenda is scored. 1[recurring-credit] Use this credit during a run.
cards.flavor: Fifteen seconds of fame.

cards.name: Paywall Implementation
cards.text: This card is not trashed until another current is played or an agenda is stolen. Gain 1[credit] whenever the Runner makes a successful run.

cards.name: Scrubbed
cards.text: This card is not trashed until another current is played or an agenda is scored. The first piece of ice encountered each turn has -2 strength for the remainder of the run.

cards.name: Sealed Vault
cards.text: 1[credit]: Move any number of credits from your credit pool to this asset. [click]: Take any number of credits from this asset. [trash]: Take any number of credits from this asset.
cards.flavor: Nothing is impenetrable. The key is to make breaking into it more costly than what it's worth.

cards.name: Targeted Marketing
cards.text: This card is not trashed until another current is played or an agenda is stolen. Name a card. Gain 10[credit] whenever the Runner plays or installs a copy of that card.

cards.name: The Foundry: Refining the Process
cards.text: The first time you rez a piece of ice each turn, you may search R&D for another copy of that ice, reveal it, and add it to HQ. Shuffle R&D.

cards.name: Three Steps Ahead
cards.text:
Play only as your first [click].
When this turn ends, gain 2[credit] for each successful run you made during it.
cards.flavor: In this business, you had to anticipate. If you weren't three steps ahead, you were three steps behind.

cards.name: Unscheduled Maintenance
cards.text: This card is not trashed until another current is played or an agenda is scored. The Corp cannot install more than 1 piece of ice each turn.
cards.flavor: What goes up must always go down.

cards.name: Will-o'-the-Wisp
cards.text: Whenever the Runner makes a successful run on this server, you may trash this upgrade. If you do, choose 1 installed icebreaker that was used to break at least 1 subroutine during this run. The Runner adds that icebreaker to the bottom of the stack.

cards.name: BlacKat
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 barrier subroutine. If you spent a credit from a stealth card to use this ability, instead break up to 3 barrier subroutines. 2[credit]: +1 strength. If you spent at least 1 credit from a stealth card to use this ability, instead +2 strength.
cards.flavor: Bad luck for any sysop blind enough to cross its path.

cards.name: Box-E
cards.text: +2[mu] Your maximum hand size is increased by 2. Limit 1 console per player.

cards.name: Chronos Project
cards.text: When you score this agenda, the Runner removes all cards in the heap from the game.
cards.flavor: The irony is that those who'd want to destroy certain memories can't afford to do so, and those who can afford it-well, they're too busy sipping on dreamwine.

cards.name: Crisium Grid
cards.text: Runs against this server cannot be declared successful. (This effect does not cause runs to become unsuccessful.) Limit 1 region per server.
cards.flavor: Mars would never have been colonized if not for the Gagarin facilities at Promontorium Agarum.

cards.name: Duggar's
cards.text: [click],[click],[click],[click]: Draw 10 cards.
cards.flavor: Carved directly out of the lunar rock, Duggar's is a popular spot among blue-collar loonies and slumming risties. A place where you could find what you're looking for-if you knew who to look for, and didn't get distracted by the energetic dancers.

cards.name: Eliza's Toybox
cards.text: [click],[click],[click]: Rez a card, ignoring all costs.
cards.flavor: Eliza's Toybox is the preeminent purveyor of high-class debauchery on the moon, courtesy of its bioroid pleasure models and other exotica. Every fantasy has its price.

cards.name: Hades Shard
cards.text: Whenever you make a successful run on Archives, instead of breaching Archives, you may install this resource from your grip, ignoring all costs. [trash]: Breach Archives. You cannot access cards in the root of Archives during this breach. Limit 1 per deck.

cards.name: IQ
cards.text:
The rez cost of IQ is increased by 1 for each card in HQ.
IQ has +1 strength for each card in HQ.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: Created by merging the brainscans of over a hundred of the most intelligent people in Haas-Bioroid's cerebral database, its effectiveness is limited either by its lack of imagination or the imagination of the sysops who employ it.

cards.name: Kitsune
cards.text: [subroutine] You may choose 1 card in HQ. If you do, the Runner breaches HQ. During this breach, the Runner cannot access cards in the root of HQ, and the first card they access must be the chosen card. When the breach ends, trash this ice.
cards.flavor: There are those who believe the nine-tailed fox is an angel in disguise. And then there are those who have followed, and discovered her secret...

cards.name: Lancelot
cards.text: When the Runner encounters this ice, you may reveal up to 2 pieces of grail ice in HQ. For the remainder of this run, this ice gains the subroutines of each revealed piece of ice in the order of your choice. [subroutine] Trash 1 installed program.
cards.flavor: He who wields the sword of valor.

cards.name: Manhunt
cards.text: This card is not trashed until another current is played or an agenda is stolen. The first time the Runner makes a successful run each turn, Trace[2]. If successful, give the Runner 1 tag.

cards.name: Order of Sol
cards.text: The first time you have no credits in your credit pool each turn, gain 1[credit].
cards.flavor: There have been several attempts to create a "world church," uniting all human faiths into a single, harmonious whole. The irony, of course, is that each new "world church" is another schism in humanity's shared religious experience.

cards.name: Port Anson Grid
cards.text: As an additional cost to jack out during a run on this server, the Runner must trash 1 installed program. Limit 1 region per server.
cards.flavor: The port was first built as a remote location to unload and offload dangerous felons.

cards.name: Quetzal: Free Spirit
cards.text: Once per turn → 0[credit]: Break 1 barrier subroutine.
cards.flavor: "Why should we be slaves to our genetic heritage?"

cards.name: Rachel Beckman
cards.text:
You get +1 allotted [click] for each of your turns.
If you are tagged, trash this resource.
cards.flavor:
"This is Rachel Beckman. She's in the business of keeping people alive."
Rachel smiled. "Only when I'm not in the business of killing them."

cards.name: Refractor
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 code gate subroutine. 1[credit]: +3 strength. Spend credits only from stealth cards to use this ability.
cards.flavor: "If you look like you belong, people will ignore you for hours. Or years. It's only when you don't fit in that things start to go wrong." -Exile

cards.name: Shattered Remains
cards.text:
Shattered Remains can be advanced.
If you pay 1[credit] when the Runner accesses Shattered Remains, trash 1 piece of hardware for each advancement token on Shattered Remains.

cards.name: The News Now Hour
cards.text: The Runner cannot play current events.
cards.flavor: "There are reports of a terrorist threat at Starport Kaguya. The NAPD is offering a reward for anyone who can provide them with information about the current whereabouts of the individual pictured here. He is considered extremely dangerous and is armed with a PAD and a portable rig."

cards.name: The Supplier
cards.text:
[click]: Host a resource or piece of hardware from your grip on The Supplier.
When your turn begins, you may install a hosted card, lowering the install cost by 2.
cards.flavor: "I can get you anything, and guarantee the best prices in town."

cards.name: Wendigo
cards.text: Wendigo can be advanced. While Wendigo has an odd number of advancement tokens on it, it gains barrier and loses code gate. [subroutine] Choose a program. The Runner cannot use the chosen program for the remainder of this run.

cards.name: Angel Arena
cards.text: Place X power counters on Angel Arena when it is installed. When there are no power counters left on Angel Arena, trash it. Hosted power counter: Reveal the top card of your stack. You may add that card to the bottom of your stack.
cards.flavor: "Low gravity sports are wildly popular, so match-fixing has proven wildly profitable." -Leela Patel

cards.name: Architect
cards.text:
Players cannot trash this ice.
[subroutine] Look at the top 5 cards of R&D. You may install 1 of those cards, ignoring the install cost.
[subroutine] You may install 1 card from Archives or HQ.
cards.flavor: Designed by 2012 World Champion Jeremy Zwirn

cards.name: Ashigaru
cards.text: This ice gains "[subroutine] End the run." for each card in HQ.
cards.flavor: The way past is to go a different way.

cards.name: Astrolabe
cards.text: +1[mu] Draw 1 card whenever the Corp creates a server. Limit 1 console per player.
cards.flavor: "There is no better tool for charting the empty spaces of the net." -Nasir Meidan

cards.name: Autoscripter
cards.text:
The first time you install a program from your grip during your turn, gain [click].
Trash Autoscripter if you make an unsuccessful run.
cards.flavor: It practically runs itself, unless you're in a pinch.

cards.name: Blue Sun: Powering the Future
cards.text: When your turn begins, you may add 1 rezzed card to HQ and gain credits equal to its rez cost.
cards.flavor: Unlimited Energy. Reasonable Prices.

cards.name: Changeling
cards.text: Changeling can be advanced. While Changeling has an odd number of advancement tokens on it, it gains sentry and loses barrier. [subroutine] End the run.

cards.name: Docklands Crackdown
cards.text:
[click], [click]: Place 1 power counter on Docklands Crackdown.
The install cost of the first card the Runner installs each turn is increased by 1 for each power counter on Docklands Crackdown.

cards.name: Fester
cards.text: Whenever the Corp purges virus counters, if the Corp has at least 2[credit], they lose 2[credit].
cards.flavor: "You should have known better than to scratch it…" -Quetzal

cards.name: Hades Fragment
cards.text:
When your turn begins, you may add 1 card from Archives to the bottom of R&D.
Limit 1 per deck.

cards.name: Inject
cards.text: Reveal the top 4 cards of your stack and trash all programs revealed. Gain 1[credit] for each program trashed, and add the rest of the revealed cards to your grip.
cards.flavor: "Knowledge comes in many different shapes and sizes." -Quetzal

cards.name: Labyrinthine Servers
cards.text: When you score this agenda, place 2 power counters on it. [interrupt] → Hosted power counter: Prevent the Runner from jacking out. The Runner cannot jack out for the remainder of this run.

cards.name: Mamba
cards.text: Hosted power counter: Do 1 net damage. Use this ability only during a run. [subroutine] Do 1 net damage. [subroutine] You and the Runner secretly spend 0[credit], 1[credit], or 2[credit]. Reveal spent credits. If you and the Runner spent a different number of credits, place 1 power counter on Mamba.

cards.name: Origami
cards.text: Your maximum hand size is increased by 1 for each copy of Origami installed.
cards.flavor: The earliest instances of data folding were inspired by the traditional art of origami. Just as a crease pattern is the blueprint of a paper crane, there is a sequence to data that must be considered in order to achieve the greatest result.

cards.name: Peak Efficiency
cards.text: Gain 1[credit] for each rezzed piece of ice.
cards.flavor: "Servers fully-armed and operational."

cards.name: Reuse
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this operation, spend [click].
Trash any number of cards from HQ. Gain 2[credit] for each card trashed.
cards.flavor: If the clones were nervous about living in a repurposed fuel tank, they never mentioned it.

cards.name: Reversed Accounts
cards.text: You can advance this asset. [click], [trash]: The Runner loses 4[credit] for each hosted advancement counter.
cards.flavor: Making a name for yourself has its perks. But it also makes you a target.

cards.name: Switchblade
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break any number of sentry subroutines. Spend credits only from stealth cards to use this ability. 1[credit]: +7 strength. Spend credits only from stealth cards to use this ability.
cards.flavor: Small. Compact. Easy to slip by monitoring programs and it can do some damage.

cards.name: Trade-In
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this event, trash an installed piece of hardware.
Gain credits equal to half the install cost of the trashed hardware (rounded down) and search your stack for a piece of hardware, reveal it, and add it to your grip. Shuffle your stack.

cards.name: Universal Connectivity Fee
cards.text: [subroutine] If the Runner is not tagged, they lose 1[credit]. If the Runner is tagged, they lose all credits in their credit pool and you trash this ice.
cards.flavor: "It's a small one-time fee, apparently. Only I've paid it seventeen times."

cards.name: Bifrost Array
cards.text: When you score Bifrost Array, you may trigger the "when scored" ability of another agenda that is not a copy of Bifrost Array in your score area.
cards.flavor: "'What does it do?' Whatever I bloody want it to do." -Director Haas

cards.name: Cerberus "Cuj.0" H3
cards.text: When you install this program, place 4 power counters on it. Interface → Hosted power counter: Break up to 2 sentry subroutines. 1[credit]: +1 strength.
cards.flavor: "He only likes to eat live meat." -MaxX

cards.name: Cerberus "Lady" H1
cards.text: When you install this program, place 4 power counters on it. Interface → Hosted power counter: Break up to 2 barrier subroutines. 1[credit]: +1 strength.
cards.flavor: "Its bytes are definitely worse than its bark." -Chaos Theory

cards.name: Cerberus "Rex" H2
cards.text: When you install this program, place 4 power counters on it. Interface → Hosted power counter: Break up to 2 code gate subroutines. 1[credit]: +1 strength.
cards.flavor: "Useful for fetching all sorts of things…but you better have a treat ready if he likes it." -Iain Stirling

cards.name: Cybsoft MacroDrive
cards.text:
1[recurring-credit]
Use this credit to install programs.
cards.flavor: Cybsoft started by designing games. Eventually they just redesigned the same game each year, and to combat piracy created a dedicated machine to play it. Profits grew ten-fold.

cards.name: Daily Business Show
cards.text: [interrupt] → The first time each turn you would draw any number of cards, increase the number of cards you will draw by 1. When you draw those cards, add 1 of them to the bottom of R&D.
cards.flavor: "A new investment deal every morning! Grab the bull by the horns and take control of your future!"

cards.name: Ekomind
cards.text: Your memory limit is equal to the number of cards in your grip. Limit 1 console per player.
cards.flavor: "Sometimes you just need a brain in a jar." -g00ru

cards.name: Executive Boot Camp
cards.text:
When your turn begins, you may rez a card, lowering the rez cost by 1[credit].
1[credit],[trash]: Search R&D for an asset, reveal it, and add it to HQ. Shuffle R&D.
cards.flavor: "Do it again, but this time I want to see you to enunciate less. Maybe let some spittle fly."

cards.name: Gemini
cards.text: [subroutine] Trace[2]. If successful, do 1 net damage. If your trace strength is 5 or greater, do 1 net damage.
cards.flavor: Gemini promised pleasure, but dealt only pain.

cards.name: Hostile Infrastructure
cards.text: Whenever the Runner trashes a Corp card (including Hostile Infrastructure), do 1 net damage.
cards.flavor: "If thou only knowest what it is to conquer, and knowest not what it is to be defeated; woe unto thee…" -Tokugawa Ieyasu

cards.name: Leela Patel: Trained Pragmatist
cards.text: Whenever an agenda is scored or stolen, add 1 unrezzed card to HQ.
cards.flavor: "I'd say I do it for the challenge, but the truth is it's not that hard."

cards.name: License Acquisition
cards.text: When you score this agenda, you may install and rez 1 asset or upgrade from HQ or Archives, ignoring all costs.
cards.flavor: "We've received seventeen crates from ChiLo. We'll hit stores the same day we sign the license agreement."

cards.name: Lycan
cards.text: Lycan can be advanced. While Lycan has an odd number of advancement tokens on it, it gains code gate and loses sentry. [subroutine] Trash 1 program.
cards.flavor: "It's weird. I hit the server again and it was like a totally different piece of ice was waiting for me. Lost my root daemon. I shouldn't have nested them seven deep."

cards.name: Merlin
cards.text: When the Runner encounters this ice, you may reveal up to 2 pieces of grail ice in HQ. For the remainder of this run, this ice gains the subroutines of each revealed piece of ice in the order of your choice. [subroutine] Do 2 net damage.
cards.flavor: He who holds the staff of wisdom.

cards.name: Sagittarius
cards.text: [subroutine] Trace[2]. If successful, trash 1 program. If your trace strength is 5 or greater, trash 1 program.
cards.flavor: Sagittarius promised foresight, but brought only regret.

cards.name: Shell Corporation
cards.text: You cannot use this upgrade more than once per turn. [click]: Place 3[credit] on this upgrade. [click]: Take all credits from this upgrade.

cards.name: Snatch and Grab
cards.text: Trace[3]. If successful, trash 1 connection. The Runner can take 1 tag to prevent this.
cards.flavor: The last thing he saw was the tattoo of a strange beast on his captor's neck. It had a goat's head, the body of a lion, and the tail of a serpent. Then the bag was yanked over his head, and there was only darkness.

cards.name: Superior Cyberwalls
cards.text: All barrier ice have +1 strength. When you score Superior Cyberwalls, gain 1[credit] for each rezzed barrier.
cards.flavor: "Our new barriers will be built on the rubble of our enemies".

cards.name: Utopia Shard
cards.text: Whenever you make a successful run on HQ, instead of breaching HQ, you may install this resource from your grip, ignoring all costs. [trash]: The Corp discards 2 cards from HQ at random. Limit 1 per deck.

cards.name: Zona Sul Shipping
cards.text:
Place 1[credit] on Zona Sul Shipping when your turn begins.
[click]: Take all credits from Zona Sul Shipping.
Trash Zona Sul Shipping if you are tagged.
cards.flavor: "They'll deliver anything to anywhere. Make sure to request air holes if you're shipping someone important, though."

cards.name: Au Revoir
cards.text: Gain 1[credit] whenever you jack out.
cards.flavor: The datastream slipped away, and it felt like being born for a second time, if only you could remember the first. A rush of air fills the lungs to bursting, and you gasp it out, coughing and choking as the dim lights of the room shine with the brilliance of a thousand suns.

cards.name: Bribery
cards.text: Make a run. During this run, the Corp must pay X[credit] as an additional cost to rez the first unrezzed piece of ice approached.
cards.flavor: "Sometimes it's helpful to remember that you're not the only one who loves money." -Gabriel Santiago

cards.name: Code Siphon
cards.text: Run R&D. If successful, instead of breaching R&D, you may search your stack for 1 program. Install it, paying 3[credit] less for each piece of ice protecting R&D, and then take 1 tag.

cards.name: Collective Consciousness
cards.text: Draw 1 card whenever the Corp rezzes a piece of ice.
cards.flavor: "All programs are connected. The data that runs through one runs through all." -Rielle "Kit" Peddler

cards.name: Earthrise Hotel
cards.text:
When you install this resource, load 3 power counters onto it. When it is empty, trash it.
When your turn begins, remove 1 hosted power counter and draw 2 cards.

cards.name: Errand Boy
cards.text:
[subroutine] The Corp gains 1[credit] or draws 1 card.
[subroutine] The Corp gains 1[credit] or draws 1 card.
[subroutine] The Corp gains 1[credit] or draws 1 card.
cards.flavor: Recycling the energy entering the system via a run is both responsible and economical.

cards.name: Excalibur
cards.text: [subroutine] The Runner cannot make another run this turn.
cards.flavor:
There drew he forth the brand Excalibur,
And o'er him, drawing it, the winter moon,
Brightening the skirts of a long cloud, ran forth
And sparkled keen with frost against the hilt:
For all the haft twinkled with diamond sparks,
Myriads of topaz-lights, and jacinth work
Of subtlest jewellery. -Lord Tennyson

cards.name: Helium-3 Deposit
cards.text: When you score Helium-3 Deposit, place up to 2 power counters on a card with at least 1 power counter on it.
cards.flavor: It takes power to create power.

cards.name: IT Department
cards.text: [click]: Place 1 power counter on IT Department. Hosted power counter: Choose a rezzed piece of ice. That ice has +1 strength until the end of the turn for each power counter (including the one spent) on IT Department.

cards.name: Incubator
cards.text: When your turn begins, place 1 virus counter on Incubator. [click], [trash]: Move all virus counters from Incubator to another installed virus program.
cards.flavor: "What terrors hatch in her dispossessed mind, waiting for their moment to be born? My money's on a double-helix rainbow with the head of a panda." -fakespeare

cards.name: Industrial Genomics: Growing Solutions
cards.text: The trash cost of each card is increased by 1 for each facedown card in Archives.
cards.flavor: Achieve the Impossible.

cards.name: Ixodidae
cards.text:
Whenever the Corp loses at least 1[credit], gain 1[credit].
Trash Ixodidae if the Corp purges virus counters.
cards.flavor: Digs in deeper than its Alabama counterpart.

cards.name: Markus 1.0
cards.text: Lose [click]: Break 1 subroutine on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. [subroutine] The Runner trashes 1 of their installed cards. [subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: The forge must never run cold.

cards.name: Sage
cards.text: This program gets +1 strength for each unused MU. Interface → 2[credit]: Break 1 code gate or 1 barrier subroutine.
cards.flavor: δὶς ἐς τὸν αὐτὸν ποταμὸν οὐκ ἂν ἐμβαίης

cards.name: Self-destruct
cards.text: Remote server only. [trash]: Trash all cards installed in the root of or protecting this server. Trace[X], where X is equal to the number of cards trashed. If successful, do 3 net damage. Use this ability only during a run on this server.

cards.name: Shoot the Moon
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this operation, spend [click].
Rez 1 piece of ice for each tag the Runner has, ignoring all costs.

cards.name: Troll
cards.text: When the Runner encounters Troll, Trace[2]. If successful, the Runner must lose [click] or end the run.
cards.flavor: You gotta pay the troll toll to get in.

cards.name: Turtlebacks
cards.text: Gain 1[credit] whenever you create a server.
cards.flavor: A masterpiece of cloning and hardware technology, Jinteki created homo vacuo operae, commonly called "turtlebacks", to operate for long periods of time within a vacuum.

cards.name: Utopia Fragment
cards.text:
As an additional cost to steal an agenda, the Runner must pay 2[credit] for each advancement token on that agenda.
Limit 1 per deck.

cards.name: Virgo
cards.text: [subroutine] Trace[2]. If successful, give the Runner 1 tag. If your trace strength is 5 or greater, give the Runner 1 tag.
cards.flavor: Virgo promised love, but offered only jealousy.

cards.name: Amped Up
cards.text: Gain [click][click][click] and suffer 1 core damage. This damage cannot be prevented.
cards.flavor: "The human brain only uses like a quarter of its capacity anyway, right?" -MaxX

cards.name: Archives Interface
cards.text: [interrupt] → Whenever you would access a card in Archives, you may instead remove it from the game. Use this ability only once each time you breach Archives.
cards.flavor: A black box that makes data disappear forever.

cards.name: Argus Security: Protection Guaranteed
cards.text: Whenever the Runner steals an agenda, they must take 1 tag or suffer 2 meat damage.
cards.flavor: We Never Sleep.

cards.name: Asteroid Belt
cards.text:
Asteroid Belt can be advanced and its rez cost is lowered by 3 for each advancement token on it.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: His belt of stone did shake and shatter.

cards.name: Builder
cards.text:
[click]: Move this piece of ice to the outermost position protecting any server.
[subroutine] Place 1 advancement token on a piece of ice protecting this server that can be advanced.
[subroutine] Place 1 advancement token on a piece of ice protecting this server that can be advanced.

cards.name: Checkpoint
cards.text:
When you rez this ice, take 1 bad publicity.
[subroutine] Trace[5]. If successful, do 3 meat damage when this run becomes successful.
cards.flavor: "I passed right through one once. It didn't seem to do anything at first. It wasn't until I jacked out that I realized they were busting down the door of my apartment." -Valencia Estevez

cards.name: Chop Bot 3000
cards.text: When your turn begins, you may trash another of your installed cards. If you do, draw 1 card or remove 1 tag.
cards.flavor: There was a sickly smell coming from his closet. He hoped it was only a mouse this time.

cards.name: Constellation Protocol
cards.text: When your turn begins, you may move an advancement token from a piece of ice to an installed piece of ice that can be advanced.
cards.flavor: "With distributed systems, assets can be realigned with no loss of efficiency." -William Knuth, The Tower of Babbage

cards.name: Cyberdex Virus Suite
cards.text: While the Runner is accessing this upgrade in R&D, they must reveal it. When the Runner accesses this upgrade, you may purge virus counters. [trash]: Purge virus counters.

cards.name: Data Folding
cards.text: When your turn begins, gain 1[credit] if you have 2 or more unused MU.
cards.flavor: "Sometimes I like to make origami cranes out of old newsrags. It helps me think, putting it back on the subconscious. I figure it's the same principle for my rig – keep it busy and it makes me a few creds for my trouble." -Quetzal

cards.name: Day Job
cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this event, spend [click][click][click].
Gain 10[credit].
cards.flavor: "Hello thank you for vidding MegaBuy I'm Carol how can I help you."

cards.name: Dedicated Technician Team
cards.text:
2[recurring-credit]
Use these credits to install ice protecting this server.
cards.flavor: Have you tried turning it off and on again?

cards.name: Eater
cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 subroutine. You cannot access cards for the remainder of this run. 1[credit]: +1 strength.
cards.flavor: Nom nom nom.

cards.name: Edward Kim: Humanity's Hammer
cards.text: Trash the first operation you access each turn at no cost.
cards.flavor: "My only regret is that androids cannot feel my hate."

cards.name: Fire Wall
cards.text:
Fire Wall can be advanced and gains +1 strength for each advancement token on it.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: "Definitely a literalist." -Liz Campbell, VP Project Security

cards.name: Firmware Updates
cards.text: When you score this agenda, place 3 agenda counters on it. Once per turn → Hosted agenda counter: Place 1 advancement counter on an installed piece of ice you can advance.

cards.name: Forked
cards.text: Run any server. The first time you fully break a sentry during that run, trash that sentry.

cards.name: Gagarin Deep Space: Expanding the Horizon
cards.text: As an additional cost to access a card in the root of a remote server, the Runner must pay 1[credit].
cards.flavor: Sic Itur Ad Astra.

cards.name: Glenn Station
cards.text:
Glenn Station can host a single card.
[click]: Host a card from HQ facedown on Glenn Station.
[click]: Add a card on Glenn Station to HQ.

cards.name: Government Takeover
cards.text:
[click]: Gain 3[credit].
Limit 1 Government Takeover per deck.
cards.flavor: It is essential to liberate a populace from tyranny before that tyranny takes root.

cards.name: Gravedigger
cards.text: Whenever an installed Corp card is trashed, place 1 virus counter on Gravedigger. [click], hosted virus counter: The Corp trashes the top card of R&D.
cards.flavor: "Once your sniffer finds the protocols the server uses to trash its own data, you can spoof those same protocols. It's quite the show." -Ji "Noise" Reilly

cards.name: High-Risk Investment
cards.text: Place 1 agenda counter on High-Risk Investment when you score it. [click], hosted agenda counter: Gain 1[credit] for each credit in the Runner's credit pool.
cards.flavor: "Trust me. I know what I'm doing."

cards.name: Hivemind
cards.text: Place 1 virus counter on Hivemind when it is installed. Virus counters on Hivemind are considered to be hosted on all other virus programs for the purposes of card effects (and can be spent as if on them).
cards.flavor: "We built the network. But then the network evolved. Can we be sure that it is not alive?" -g00ru

cards.name: Housekeeping
cards.text: This operation is not trashed until another current is played or an agenda is stolen. The first time each turn the Runner installs a card, they trash 1 card from the grip.

cards.name: Human First
cards.text: Whenever an agenda is scored or stolen, gain credits equal to the agenda points on that agenda.
cards.flavor: "They showed me that I wasn't broken. I am still a whole human, no matter how many limbs I lose. The golems are our enemy, as well as anyone who values efficiency and profit more than a human life." -Edward Kim

cards.name: I've Had Worse
cards.text:
Draw 3 cards.
Whenever I've Had Worse is trashed by taking net or meat damage, draw 3 cards.

cards.name: Investigative Journalism
cards.text: Install only if the Corp has at least 1 bad publicity. [click][click][click][click], [trash]: Give the Corp 1 bad publicity.
cards.flavor: Her heart beat faster as her reader illuminated the records. It was all there. The pod had not been reprogrammed since the 14th, which meant that this was a case of gross negligence.

cards.name: Itinerant Protesters
cards.text: This event is not trashed until another current is played or an agenda is scored. The Corp gets −1 maximum hand size for each bad publicity they have.
cards.flavor: No one knows what they want-least of all them.

cards.name: Knifed
cards.text: Run any server. The first time you fully break a barrier during that run, trash that barrier.

cards.name: Mark Yale
cards.text: Whenever you spend an agenda counter, gain 1[credit]. [trash] or any agenda counter: Gain 2[credit].
cards.flavor: "This is a one-of-a-kind opportunity…"

cards.name: MaxX: Maximum Punk Rock
cards.text: When your turn begins, trash the top 2 cards of your stack. Draw 1 card.

cards.name: MemStrips
cards.text: +3[mu] Use the MU on MemStrips only for virus programs.
cards.flavor: "The trick is remembering which virus you loaded onto which strip. That's why I draw emoji on 'em. Then I just have to remember which emoji stands for which virus." -Princess Space Kitten

cards.name: Nebula
cards.text:
Nebula can be advanced and its rez cost is lowered by 3 for each advancement token on it.
[subroutine] Trash 1 program.
cards.flavor: He bent his bow of stellar matter.

cards.name: Orion
cards.text:
Orion can be advanced and its rez cost is lowered by 3 for each advancement token on it.
[subroutine] Trash 1 program.
[subroutine] Resolve a subroutine on another piece of rezzed ice.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.flavor: And seeking prey he then took aim.

cards.name: Patch
cards.text: Install Patch on a rezzed piece of ice as a hosted condition counter with the text "Host ice has +2 strength."
cards.flavor:
Update 1.1:
-Fixes some stability issues. //maybe

cards.name: Progenitor
cards.text: You can install virus programs onto this program. Limit 1 hosted program. The memory cost of the hosted program does not count against your memory limit. [interrupt] → Whenever virus counters would be purged, prevent 1 virus counter on the hosted program from being removed.

cards.name: Qianju PT
cards.text: When your turn begins, you may lose [click]. If you do, the first time you would take tags from now until your next turn begins, prevent 1 tag.
cards.flavor: "By the time you add in all of the options, you've spent about three times the base price. Of course, a lot of the systems are supposed to make you safer - if you can keep track of them."

cards.name: Sacrificial Clone
cards.text: [interrupt] → [trash]: Prevent all damage. Trash all installed hardware, all installed non-virtual resources, and all cards from your grip. Lose all credits in your credit pool. Remove all tags.
cards.flavor: "Don't worry, me. You won't have to vertical park." -Ji "Noise" Reilly

cards.name: Satellite Grid
cards.text: Each piece of ice protecting this server is considered to have 1 additional advancement token on it. Limit 1 region per server.

cards.name: Searchlight
